mechanisms.title: Mechanical documentation synchronization gates
mechanisms.problem: Documentation examples, command lists and formatting drift from code and are usually reviewed only by reading.
triggers: documentation contains TypeScript fences, command inventories or taxonomy tables
a doc or its referenced API changes
local hooks and CI need the same doc checks at different depths
obligations: Verify executable examples instead of authoring a second generated copy when the check is cheap and exact.
Cap silent opt-outs: more than half of fenced examples carrying an ignore annotation fails the gate.
Render each prose paragraph as one physical line so review diffs stay attributable.
Expose one shared doc-sync aggregate; local use may select surfaces, CI runs the exhaustive set.
steps: Run the doc-sync aggregate in check mode before committing.
Compile extracted TypeScript fences against the real project and report file:line diagnostics.
Count ignore-check annotations and fail when the ratio exceeds the threshold.
Run the markdown wrap check and rewrite offending paragraphs; never auto-rewrite mixed changes silently.
In CI invoke the exhaustive aggregate rather than a hand-copied command chain.

enforcement.implementation: doc-sync scripts registered in the hygiene/CI aggregate
enforcement.trust: Gate output is authoritative only for the encoded surfaces; taxonomy checks were later superseded by a generated catalog, so do not treat the original list as complete truth.
enforcement.failure: Nonzero exit with per-file diagnostics; ratio overrun and non-wrapped paragraphs block.
enforcement.exceptions: A fence may opt out with an explicit ignore annotation, bounded by the ratio cap; a generated catalog fence is excluded from the typecheck ratio because the generator owns its freshness.

mechanisms.applicability: Repositories whose docs contain compilable examples, canonical command lists or taxonomy tables; the ratio parameter and aggregate name must be re-derived per project.

migration.strategy: Introduce checks one surface at a time behind a shared aggregate, ratchet existing violations, then make CI exhaustive.
migration.implementation: Extract fences with the existing doc tooling; reuse the project's compiler; keep the ignore budget visible.
migration.requiredSupport: A doc-sync entry point, parser for the doc dialect, and CI lane.

positive: A valid fenced example compiles and the aggregate passes.
A paragraph split across physical lines is rejected.
rejection: An invalid fence fails with its source location.
A corpus where most fences are ignored fails the ratio check.
recovery: Fix the fence or remove the ignore annotation and rerun only the aggregate.

limitations: Does not prove prose accuracy or that examples cover real entry points.
The taxonomy half is historical; a generated catalog owns current taxonomy truth.
Local selective runs can miss checks that CI would run.

mechanisms.title: Evidence-based build-tool replacement
mechanisms.problem: Replacing a build tool on novelty creates maintenance risk and hidden output-shape changes.
triggers: a build tool is slow, unmaintained or blocks a needed capability
obligations: Justify the switch with maintenance evidence: downloads, maintainer count, bus factor and upgrade risk.
Switch at the lowest-cost moment, before publishing or at a natural cutover.
Narrow workspace globs explicitly and record per-package overrides in the vendor/ownership ledger.
Preserve output shape (entry names, declaration layout) so consumers do not change.
steps: Collect comparable maintenance and feature evidence for both tools.
Prototype the replacement on the smallest workspace surface and compare emitted files.
Record overrides and vendor modifications in the owning README.
Cut over in one change, remove the old tool configuration, and keep verification of output shape.

enforcement.trust: Evidence is self-reported by the author; reviewers must check download/maintainer facts and emitted shape.
enforcement.failure: A switch without evidence or with changed output shape is rejected in review.
enforcement.exceptions: A product-specific choice is not a universal mandate; the transferable rule is the evidence and cutover procedure.

mechanisms.applicability: Any project considering a build/test tool replacement; numeric thresholds are project-specific.

migration.strategy: Adopt the evidence template, not the specific tool.
migration.implementation: Compare emitted artifacts and configuration surface, then cut over once.
migration.requiredSupport: Owner for build config and a representative consumer.

positive: Prototype emits byte-compatible entry points and declarations.
rejection: A proposal lacking maintenance evidence or changing output shape is blocked.
recovery: Revert to the previous tool config and keep the comparison as evidence.

limitations: Maintenance metrics age; re-evaluate on major upgrades.
The source choice (tsdown) is not itself transferable.

mechanisms.title: Vendored source provenance manifest
mechanisms.problem: Vendored upstream source silently diverges from its recorded origin and local modifications become untraceable.
triggers: third-party source is copied into the repository
obligations: Record the upstream repository and exact commit for every vendored package.
Log every local modification and its reason in an owning manifest.
Reject a commit that changes vendored source without updating the manifest in the same commit.
Pin workspace resolution to the vendored copy and exclude it from rules that would rewrite upstream style.
steps: Add the package with upstream path, ref and SHA.
Apply local patches and append each to the modification log.
Install the pre-commit guard that compares changed paths to manifest updates.
Re-sync by replacing source at a new SHA and re-applying the logged patches.

enforcement.trust: The hook proves only that the manifest changed; a human must verify the claim matches upstream.
enforcement.failure: Commit rejected when vendored paths change without a manifest update.
enforcement.exceptions: Read-only documentation files and generated notices may be exempt by explicit path rules.

mechanisms.applicability: Projects that vendor dependencies or embed upstream source; the manifest format and hook are adaptable.

migration.strategy: Add the manifest first for existing vendored trees, then enable the guard after the log is complete.
migration.implementation: Use a checked-in manifest plus a path-based hook; keep patches as files if drift verification is planned.
migration.requiredSupport: VCS hooks and an ownership doc.

positive: A vendored change with a matching manifest entry commits.
rejection: A vendored change without a manifest update is rejected.
recovery: Update the manifest, restage both files and retry.

limitations: Forward-direction only unless an external drift check reconstructs upstream.
Does not prove the logged modification text is complete.

mechanisms.title: Single compiler and project-reference ownership
mechanisms.problem: Multiple transpilers produce divergent typing, declaration and runtime behavior.
triggers: TypeScript is built, bundled or tested
obligations: Let one TypeScript compiler own type checking, transforms and declaration emit.
Express per-directory strictness through project references, not separate compiler pipelines.
Verify published declaration specifiers from an external consumer's perspective before release.
Keep a build order: compiler first, then bundling; never let a second tool decide module/type semantics.
steps: Declare each package in exactly one aggregate reference graph.
Run `tsc -b` for the face before any bundler stage.
Use per-package tsconfig only to narrow include/strictness, not to fork transforms.
Run the external declaration-specifier check against packed output.

enforcement.implementation: tsc project references, build scripts, declaration-consumer test
enforcement.trust: Compiler output is authoritative; a bundler config that re-emits declarations is a defect.
enforcement.failure: Typecheck/build fails on missing references or invalid specifiers.
enforcement.exceptions: A generated file or vendor tree may be excluded from the graph with an explicit owner.

mechanisms.applicability: TypeScript monorepos with multiple build faces; command names and aggregate shape vary.

migration.strategy: Collapse duplicate transforms into `tsc` first, then make bundlers consume emitted files.
migration.implementation: Introduce project references and one aggregate per face; delete the old compiler path.
migration.requiredSupport: TypeScript project-reference graph and CI typecheck lane.

positive: A clean build emits declarations consumed by an external fixture.
rejection: A second declaration emitter or missing reference fails.
recovery: Add the missing reference and rebuild from the aggregate.

limitations: Archived decision; later notes change command order but not ownership.
Generated type metadata may require a separate analyzer.

mechanisms.title: Clean commands derive targets and refuse unsafe deletion
mechanisms.problem: A clean command that guesses directories can delete source or dependencies outside the build.
obligations: Derive deletion targets from the live reference graph and known output directories.
Refuse deletion when a resolved parent escapes the repository.
Preserve `node_modules` for existing manifests and refuse unknown files in manifest-less directories.
Never run clean automatically as part of install or unrelated commands.
steps: Resolve each package through the build graph.
Compare each target to the repository root and refuse escapes.
Delete only known generated outputs; stop on unknown files.
Print the targets and require an explicit clean invocation.

enforcement.trust: Guard behavior is deterministic but filesystem races remain; a human confirms broad cleans.
enforcement.failure: Clean aborts before deleting an unsafe path.
enforcement.exceptions: An explicit force flag may exist, but it must be documented and never used by default.

mechanisms.applicability: Any project with a destructive clean script.

migration.strategy: Replace glob-based deletion with graph-derived targets, add refusals before enabling.
migration.implementation: Compute targets from manifests/references; add containment checks.
migration.requiredSupport: Build graph and package manifest reader.

positive: Clean removes only generated outputs and preserves node_modules.
rejection: A symlink or parent escaping the repo aborts the clean.
recovery: Restore files from version control and fix the target derivation.

limitations: Cannot protect against a human running raw rm.
Concurrent writers can still race after the guard.

mechanisms.title: Path-encoded decision-note classification
mechanisms.problem: Lifecycle and kind of decision notes are ambiguous when stored as free-form files.
triggers: a decision note is created or moved
obligations: Encode lifecycle and class in the path as a closed set.
Reject loose files, unknown class folders and centralized indexes.
Keep canonical class sets in code and amend them deliberately.
Scan code comments for root-relative note/doc references and assert the target exists.
steps: Choose lifecycle (`proposed|implemented|archived`) and class from the canonical set.
Place the file under the matching directory.
Run the classification gate; fix rejected paths instead of adding an index.
When a note moves lifecycle, move the file and update links.

enforcement.trust: Path is authoritative; the gate does not judge content quality.
enforcement.failure: Unknown folder or loose note fails; a dangling doc/note reference fails.
enforcement.exceptions: Pre-format historical notes may be grandfathered by explicit date rules.

mechanisms.applicability: Repositories using durable decision records; class names are local policy.

migration.strategy: Define the closed sets in one module, then migrate existing notes with a script.
migration.implementation: Validate directories, filenames and references.
migration.requiredSupport: CI and a canonical class registry.

positive: A correctly placed note and its reference pass.
rejection: An unknown class directory or loose note fails.
recovery: Move the note and update references.

limitations: Does not verify the note's claims or that the chosen class fits.
Reference scan is path-based and misses prose mentions.

mechanisms.title: Generated reference catalogs with drift checks
mechanisms.problem: Hand-maintained catalogs of APIs or plugin surfaces drift and can be gamed by partial checks.
triggers: a machine-readable surface exists in AST/config
obligations: Generate when the AST/config is the complete truth; verify when extraction cannot be complete.
Require an explicit mode tag and structurally cross-check it.
Fail closed on unmapped types with named, reviewed exceptions.
Mark the generated fence so doc typechecking skips it, and run `--write`/`--check` freshness in the shared gate.
steps: Run the generator in check mode from real source.
Fail on unknown/ambiguous entries rather than dropping them.
Commit the generated artifact and let CI compare bytes.
Regenerate after changing the source surface; never edit the fence by hand.

enforcement.trust: Deterministic output is trusted for coverage, not for semantic correctness of prose.
enforcement.failure: Stale or structurally incomplete catalog fails.
enforcement.exceptions: Curated pinned-vendor tables may be tiered separately when extraction cannot see the source.

mechanisms.applicability: Docs or inventories derived from code; generator language and paths vary.

migration.strategy: Start with the most complete surface, add a drift check, then expand.
migration.implementation: Emit a deterministic file; expose write/check modes; exclude its fence from typechecking.

positive: Regeneration produces byte-identical output.
rejection: A hand edit or stale artifact fails the check.
recovery: Run `--write` and review the byte diff.

limitations: A complete-looking generator can still omit runtime-constructed entries.
Historical taxonomy gates may no longer cover the current surface.

mechanisms.title: Boot-and-harvest runtime surface catalog
mechanisms.problem: Static analysis cannot faithfully enumerate schemas assembled at runtime.
triggers: docs need a complete runtime inventory
obligations: Boot the real registry and harvest registered schemas instead of parsing source.
Glob every candidate package and fail when one is absent from the manifest.
Keep the boot recipe hand-written and reviewable.
Make output deterministic and check freshness in doc-sync.
steps: Start the registry in a controlled environment.
Collect every registered schema and its package identity.
Compare the package glob to harvested entries and hard-error on omissions.
Write the catalog; commit; CI checks bytes.

enforcement.implementation: boot harness + completeness guard + freshness check
enforcement.trust: Runtime registration is authoritative; the boot recipe itself is policy and may omit non-default plugins deliberately.
enforcement.failure: Missing package or non-deterministic output fails.
enforcement.exceptions: A package may be excluded only through an explicit boot-recipe decision.

mechanisms.applicability: Plugin/tool systems with runtime registration.

migration.strategy: Add the boot harness before replacing any hand list, then delete the list.
migration.implementation: Run in CI with a hermetic config and deterministic serializer.

positive: All registered tools appear in the catalog.
rejection: A tool package missing from the boot manifest fails.
recovery: Fix registration or the explicit exclusion, regenerate.

limitations: Only sees code paths the boot recipe executes.
Does not prove each schema is usable.

mechanisms.title: Uniform decision-note format gate
mechanisms.problem: Free-form notes make lifecycle, status and rationale impossible to audit consistently.
triggers: a note is added or edited
obligations: Require H1 plus a dateless Status consistent with the folder.
Apply a per-lifecycle body skeleton and ban proposal-era headings in implemented notes.
Require an alternatives section; permit an explicit grandfather comment only for pre-format dates, never invent rationale.
Normalize the whole corpus in one migration rather than maintaining two formats.
steps: Validate heading/status/folder agreement.
Validate required and forbidden headings for the lifecycle.
Fail on missing alternatives unless the grandfather marker is valid for the note date.
Use the formatter only in check mode in CI; humans write the content.

enforcement.trust: Mechanical structure only; reviewers judge content.
enforcement.failure: Missing heading, wrong status or missing alternatives fails.
enforcement.exceptions: Grandfather comment for pre-format notes; free-form technical sections allowed under canonical headings.

mechanisms.applicability: Any decision-record corpus with lifecycle states.

migration.strategy: Normalize the corpus once, then enable the gate with a date-based grandfather rule.
migration.implementation: Parse headings and front matter; keep a single formatter.

positive: A conforming note passes.
rejection: A proposal heading in an implemented note fails.
recovery: Rewrite the section or correct the status.

limitations: Cannot detect invented alternatives with a valid heading.
Format gate does not check factual accuracy.

mechanisms.title: Exported-API documentation gate
mechanisms.problem: Public exports lack documentation and reviewers cannot enforce coverage manually.
triggers: a public export is added or changed
obligations: Share one definition of 'documented' between the catalog and the gate.
Cover each declaration kind including namespaces, re-exports and `export =`.
Fail closed on unknown declaration kinds.
Record explicit exemption families and fill the adoption baseline in the same change.
steps: Run the gate over the public surface.
Resolve heritage/type-checker-based documentation rather than name matching.
Report each undocumented export with its location.
Fill documentation or add a reviewed exemption; rerun.

enforcement.trust: Compiler usage determines documentation inheritance; reserved-name blind spots remain.
enforcement.failure: Any undocumented export outside exemptions fails.
enforcement.exceptions: Three explicit exemption families; constructor property parameters and similar are covered by rules.

mechanisms.applicability: TypeScript libraries with a published API.

migration.strategy: Baseline existing gaps, fill them in one change, then block new gaps.
migration.implementation: Use the compiler API; share the documented predicate with docs generation.

positive: A documented export passes; inherited docs count.
rejection: A new undocumented export fails.
recovery: Add a doc comment or a reviewed exemption.

limitations: Reserved-name and dynamic-export forms can escape.

mechanisms.title: Required CI lanes and aggregate verdict
mechanisms.problem: Parallel CI can omit work while the required aggregate stays green.
obligations: Give each platform/face a named lane with an explicit gate inventory.
Make the required aggregate depend on every blocking lane.
Reject missing or duplicate shard assignments.
Validate publication views structurally without repacking in each lane.
steps: Declare lanes and their inventories in code.
Run the aggregate over all required lanes.
Fail on missing/duplicate gates and on an incomplete matrix.
Keep diagnostic lanes outside the required aggregate.

enforcement.trust: Workflow specs and inventory tests, not prose, are the source of truth.
enforcement.failure: Missing lane or incomplete aggregate blocks merge.
enforcement.exceptions: Diagnostic/master-only lanes intentionally do not feed branch protection.

mechanisms.applicability: Any multi-lane CI with a single merge gate.

migration.strategy: Enumerate blocking lanes first, then build one aggregate and test the inventory.
migration.implementation: Use workflow specs to pin lane membership.

positive: All required lanes pass and the aggregate is green.
rejection: A missing lane or duplicate shard fails the aggregate.
recovery: Restore the lane inventory and rerun.

limitations: Historical topology superseded by later runner evidence; principles remain.
Aggregate cannot prove a lane tested the right thing.

mechanisms.title: Declarative gate scheduler with one leaf inventory
mechanisms.problem: Command chains duplicate gate lists and spawn one process per wrapper, hiding drift and latency.
triggers: local hooks and CI both invoke them
obligations: Make one declared leaf inventory the single source of truth for each mode.
Reject invalid or ambiguous dependency graphs before spawning.
Distinguish `needs` from `after`; `allowFailure` reports without failing the aggregate.
Stream output only for coordinators with attributable subprocesses; buffer per-gate output deterministically.
Bound concurrency by measured resource cost (e.g., each doc gate builds a Program), not by CPU count alone.
steps: Declare modes and leaves in the scheduler module.
Validate the graph and duplicate names before execution.
Run ready gates up to the concurrency limit, respecting dependencies.
Print a stable summary line per gate; consumers parse that, not interleaved logs.
Add a gate by editing the inventory once; tests pin the set.

enforcement.trust: Inventory tests pin membership; subprocess exit codes remain the signal.
enforcement.failure: Invalid graph, missing leaf or failing required gate fails the run.
enforcement.exceptions: `allowFailure` gates report status without failing; a leaf may be excluded by mode.

mechanisms.applicability: Monorepos with many checks and both local/CI invocation.

migration.strategy: Replace the longest `&&` chain first, keep leaf commands unchanged, then unify inventories.
migration.implementation: Implement `needs`/`after`, buffered output and a summary line; pin with tests.
migration.requiredSupport: Process spawner and CI summary parser.

positive: A mode runs exactly its declared leaves and honors dependencies.
rejection: A duplicate or unknown leaf name aborts before spawn.
recovery: Fix the inventory and rerun only the failed leaf.

limitations: Buffered output can hide progress; coordinators need explicit streaming.

mechanisms.title: Single-source documentation site projection
mechanisms.problem: Published docs fork from their canonical location and drift, or the site owns a second copy.
triggers: docs are published to a site
source paths and public URLs differ
a release tag should publish docs
obligations: Keep canonical docs in their owning tier and define an explicit publication manifest.
Project into a disposable tree before rendering; never edit the copy.
Rewrite links and fail on missing targets.
Reject site Markdown outside the projection.
Build production docs in doc-sync but publish from a separate release-triggered workflow; derive base paths from host metadata.
steps: Map each source file to a stable public route.
Project into a temporary directory with front matter controlling edit links.
Render and validate internal links.
Publish only from the release workflow/tag, never from an arbitrary branch.

enforcement.implementation: projection script + link/layout gates + release workflow
enforcement.trust: Manifest and source remain authoritative; the rendered site is disposable.
enforcement.failure: Missing link target, stray site file or failed production build blocks publication.
enforcement.exceptions: External links and generated assets need explicit handling; base path is host-provided.

mechanisms.applicability: Projects publishing owned docs to a site generator.

migration.strategy: Create the manifest for existing pages before deleting site-local copies.
migration.implementation: Copy to a temp tree, rewrite links, validate, render.

positive: A source page renders at its declared route with working links.
rejection: A site-only Markdown file or broken internal link fails.
recovery: Fix the manifest/source and regenerate the temporary tree.

limitations: Host-specific routing/base-path rules must be parameterized.

mechanisms.title: Program-backed semantic gates
mechanisms.problem: Name- and syntax-based checks miss type-level relationships and produce false confidence.
triggers: a rule is about assignability, registrations or API compatibility
obligations: Build one no-emit Program from the complete solution graph; never let a gate assemble a partial Program.
Use the type checker for assignability/heritage instead of naming conventions.
Treat only finite literal sets as closed; generic forwarding is attributed to call sites.
Prove locality with a full-index fallback: optimization must not change results.
Require every declared event/registration to have a discovered producer; fail on ambiguity.
steps: Expand the solution references into one Program.
Run the semantic query and collect concrete locations.
If a local proof is used, fall back to a full index when it cannot prove coverage.
Report missing, widened, stale or ambiguous cases with file:line.

enforcement.trust: The Program is authoritative for the loaded graph; unsupported annotations must be reserved and validated.
enforcement.failure: Any unproven/missing producer or widened type fails.
enforcement.exceptions: Explicitly reserved annotations may carry a reviewed classification.

mechanisms.applicability: TypeScript systems with registration maps or API surfaces.

migration.strategy: Start from one complete aggregate, then add semantic rules.
migration.implementation: Reuse the compiler Program; avoid partial per-package programs.
migration.requiredSupport: Compiler API and a stable graph.

positive: A correctly assigned type passes from a real call site.
rejection: A missing producer or widened type fails.
recovery: Fix the registration/type and rerun with a clean Program.

mechanisms.title: Layer-owned test evidence
mechanisms.problem: GUI tests duplicate lower-layer assertions or mock away the behavior they claim to prove.
triggers: a feature spans unit, Host and browser layers
a transport or UI bug is fixed
obligations: Cut tiers along architectural hooks; each tier tests only its layer.
State in a lane map when each tier must run.
Do not call an in-process mock all-green done when real carrier semantics differ.
Reconcile a red case against the contract immediately instead of loosening the test.
steps: Identify the layer that owns the behavior.
Add the assertion at that layer and avoid re-testing lower layers above.
Run the lane map required for the touched surface.
If the real carrier is touched, run the browser/transport lane.

enforcement.trust: Green tests are evidence only for the layer actually exercised.
enforcement.failure: A change touching transport without the real lane is incomplete.
enforcement.exceptions: An explicit skip requires a tracked reason and owning layer.

mechanisms.applicability: Applications with UI plus host/runtime layers.

migration.strategy: Define layers from existing architectural boundaries, then move assertions down.
migration.implementation: Document the lane map and make it reviewable.

positive: A bug reproduces in the owning layer and is fixed there.
rejection: A higher-layer mock test alone does not qualify.
recovery: Add the missing real-carrier test.

limitations: Real browser/runtime tests are slow and environment-dependent.

mechanisms.title: Regression pinning at the owning test
mechanisms.problem: Bug fixes without a reproducing assertion regress silently.
obligations: Add or strengthen an assertion in the owning spec before or with the fix.
Prove the assertion fails without the fix when feasible.
Keep the pin at the lowest layer that reproduces the defect.
steps: Reproduce the defect in the owning test.
Make the test fail for the expected reason.
Apply the fix and keep the assertion.
Reference the issue/PR in the test or commit.

enforcement.trust: Reviewer must see the failing-then-passing evidence; CI only proves the final state.
enforcement.failure: A fix without a pin is sent back.
enforcement.exceptions: Pure refactors or unreachable-environment defects may use a documented alternative.

mechanisms.applicability: All bug fixes.

migration.strategy: Adopt as review policy, then add a checklist item.
migration.implementation: No tooling required beyond test ownership.

positive: The new assertion fails on the parent commit and passes with the fix.
rejection: A fix with no pin is rejected.
recovery: Add the reproducer and rerun the owning suite.

limitations: Not every defect is cheaply reproducible.
Review evidence is not automatically archived.

mechanisms.title: Capacity decisions from exact-head benchmarks
mechanisms.problem: Runner or infrastructure size is changed from core counts or intuition, not observed performance.
triggers: CI capacity/topology is proposed to change
obligations: Measure exact-head complete jobs across candidate sizes, including setup/cache and observed hardware.

For controlled preview sizing, hold checkout SHA, lockfile, Node/pnpm versions and full workspace build plus preview/VFS packing commands constant; start every runner without build outputs. Cold installs restore no dependency cache (bootstrap files may exist); warm installs restore the same exact cache without prefix fallback. This conditional benchmark rule does not replace ordinary PR cache fallback policy.

Record actual image, CPU, RAM, disk, cache outcome, phase duration, exit status and peak memory. GNU time maximum RSS is a process maximum, not simultaneous aggregate memory across the build process tree.

Estimate gross compute by summing ceil(elapsed minutes) times that runner's rate for each completed job, including setup, restore, cleanup, failed jobs and measurement uploads; report seed jobs separately. Queue delay is latency, not execution. Included minutes and storage are separate; estimates are not invoice totals.

A build-only benchmark neither deploys nor accesses Cloudflare credentials nor posts PR comments; it cannot prove complete preview publication cost, deployment latency or protected-image delivery. Confirm the selected runner through the actual preview workflow.

Changing the preview runner preserves PR events, per-PR cancellation, immutable install, restore-only dependency caching, full workspace build, preview packing, sourcemap removal and preview-page placement at the deployment root. Upload only the built site to the PR branch alias; check protected images for HTTP 200, absent transport content encoding and gzip magic bytes; keep URL comments idempotent and Dependabot/other PR authors on GitHub-hosted runners.
Treat timing targets as observations, not cancellation deadlines or correctness criteria.
Keep inner worker and outer job concurrency separate and bound them by determinism.
Remove dormant alternative topologies; pre-wire failover with one repository variable and a drill.
steps: Collect complete-job timings at several sizes.
Compare medians and variance, not one sample.

For a controlled preview comparison, retain clean-output and exact-cache evidence and the per-job accounting table; separate seed jobs, queue delay, included minutes and storage from the compute estimate.

Reviewer checks constant build/packing/toolchain inputs, attribution limits and conserved preview phases. Reject aggregate-only rounding, omitted failed/overhead jobs, warm prefix fallback or publication claims based on build-only runs; author corrects the inputs/accounting and re-runs the comparison before runner approval.
Choose the smallest size that meets the observed target without breaking determinism.
Document the failover variable and drill it; remove unused topologies.

enforcement.trust: Measurements are samples; reviewers check methodology, hardware, per-job cost accounting and instrument attribution. Build-only observations are not publication evidence; no real target runner experiment is supplied by this package.
enforcement.failure: Reject a capacity change without evidence, a controlled preview experiment with unequal inputs or cache fallback, incomplete/aggregate-rounded costs, or a build-only publication claim. Restore the selector or correct and remeasure before approval.
enforcement.exceptions: Emergency failover may temporarily override, with a drill and rollback.

mechanisms.applicability: CI fleet and runner sizing decisions.

migration.strategy: Record a baseline before changing capacity, then measure the candidate.
migration.implementation: Use workflow timestamps/logs and observed runner rates; retain the conditional controlled-preview protocol and per-job accounting in the capacity reference. Assign a real CI owner and reviewer, attach records to the target's existing runner-change review, and exercise the actual preview before claiming publication verified. No new benchmark runner, credentials or automatic cost gate is implied.

positive: Candidate size meets the target with complete-job timing.
rejection: Core-count inference or incomplete timing is rejected.
recovery: Re-run the baseline and restore the previous selector.

limitations: Benchmarks are not correctness proof; GNU-time maximum RSS is not aggregate process-tree memory. Build-only cost excludes publication proof and gross compute estimates are not invoice totals. The package delivers a review procedure, not a real target experiment or enforced automatic cost validator. Preservation repair independently reviewed correct: _working/audit/preview-sizing-repaired-source-independent.json resolved F1/F2 as resolved-retained with no new defects, 33 reference/10 knowledge discriminators present and a 20-case reviewer-decision exercise (4 accept/16 reject) — a hypothetical review exercise, not a real runner measurement.
mechanisms.sourceLifecycle: mixed: archived runner decision and current preview-sizing EN/ZH instructions

mechanisms.title: Tiered local hooks versus exhaustive CI
mechanisms.problem: Pre-commit hooks duplicate CI and become slow, or local evidence is mistaken for full coverage.
obligations: Keep pre-commit to cheap, high-confidence checks; move exhaustive suites/builds to CI once per revision.
Run the narrowly covering evidence once locally and let reviewers judge selection.
Reserve full local rehearsal for explicit requests, CI diagnosis or repo-wide changes.
Observe hook latency rather than enforcing it with a timing test.
steps: Run staged lint/whitespace/vendor guards in pre-commit.
Run incremental typecheck in pre-push if configured.
For changes, run the narrowest suite that covers the touched layer.
Rely on CI for the exhaustive matrix; never claim local runs equal it.

enforcement.trust: Hooks can be skipped; CI is the blocking evidence.
enforcement.failure: Hook failure blocks the commit; CI failure blocks merge.
enforcement.exceptions: A full local rehearsal may be requested; hook bypass must be visible.

mechanisms.applicability: Repositories with expensive exhaustive matrices.

migration.strategy: Measure current hook cost, keep only defects catchable cheaply, move the rest to CI.
migration.implementation: Use staged-file scoping and incremental builds.

positive: A staged whitespace defect is caught before commit.
rejection: An exhaustive suite is not claimed from a narrow local run.
recovery: Fix locally or let CI provide the full result.

limitations: Agents may over- or under-select local tests.

mechanisms.title: Product-first root README maintenance
mechanisms.problem: The root README grows into a duplicate manual or drifts from commands and release stage.
triggers: commands, entry points, release stage or capability families change
obligations: Keep the root README a compact product/contributor entry point.
Preserve accurate reviewed wording and distinguish factual refresh from editorial rewrite.
Update it when commands, entry points, release-stage claims or capability families change.
Link detail to owned guides; do not duplicate the documentation site home.
steps: Check the claim against the owning guide/command.
Make the minimal factual edit or link change.
Avoid restating detailed procedures.
Review for accidental scope expansion.

enforcement.trust: No automatic checker; reviewer validates claims.
enforcement.failure: Stale commands or duplicated manual content are review findings.
enforcement.exceptions: A major product repositioning may justify a larger rewrite.

mechanisms.applicability: Any root README used as an entry point.

migration.strategy: Trim to entry-point scope and link details out.
migration.implementation: Assign an owner and a change trigger list.

positive: Changed command is reflected and linked guide owns detail.
rejection: A stale command remains after a CLI change.
recovery: Correct the claim and link the owning guide.

mechanisms.title: Solution root with two explicit aggregate Programs
mechanisms.problem: A single tsconfig root mixes Host and Client environments or silently drops files.
triggers: the repository has multiple compiler faces
declaration merging or DOM/Node libs collide
obligations: Keep a program-less solution root referencing explicit aggregate programs.
Do not build the solution root directly; seed an aggregate.
Register each package in exactly one aggregate.
Keep Host and Client phases serial when generated contracts flow between them.
steps: Add the package to the correct aggregate's references.
Run the face aggregate rather than the root.
Keep shared base config free of include/files.
Verify declaration-merge collisions only inside a Program.

enforcement.trust: The aggregate is authoritative; the root is navigation only.
enforcement.failure: Missing aggregate membership or direct root build produces incomplete diagnostics.
enforcement.exceptions: A shared config may hold compiler options but not inputs.

mechanisms.applicability: TypeScript monorepos with browser and host faces.

migration.strategy: Split the root into a solution plus face aggregates, then move packages.
migration.implementation: Delete duplicate build configs; pin membership.

positive: Each package is typechecked in its face aggregate.
rejection: A package only reachable from the root is not checked.
recovery: Add it to one aggregate and rerun.

limitations: Generated contract order must be maintained.

mechanisms.title: Demo capture with explicit provenance
mechanisms.problem: Recorded demos silently switch between real, fixture-backed and simulated flows, so evidence overstates what was exercised.
triggers: a demo/GIF is recorded for review
a flow has prerequisites the environment lacks
obligations: Establish and state whether the flow is real, fixture-backed or simulated; never silently downgrade.
Report missing prerequisites instead of substituting a fixture.
Capture semantic storyboard states and verify the encoded output (e.g., ffprobe).
Keep recording local/side-effect-free; separate attachment authorization from recording.
Keep frames in a gitignored tool root, not the PR branch.
steps: Check prerequisites (server, key, model) and record the provenance decision.
Drive the real flow and capture storyboard states.
Encode deterministically and validate the file with a probe.
Attach only when the task authorizes it; otherwise keep the local recording.

enforcement.implementation: recorder tool + provenance note in the PR
enforcement.trust: The recorder reports what it can establish; reviewers must not treat a fixture demo as real behavior.
enforcement.failure: Missing prerequisites stop the run; a mislabeled provenance is a review failure.
enforcement.exceptions: Fixture flow only when the user explicitly requested it, labeled as such.

mechanisms.applicability: UI/product demos used as PR evidence.

migration.strategy: Make provenance a required output field and fail when not established.
migration.implementation: Probe prerequisites, record state transitions, validate encoding.

positive: Real flow recording states provenance and passes media probe.
rejection: A fixture run labeled real is rejected; missing prerequisite aborts.
recovery: Provide the prerequisite or record with an explicit fixture label.

limitations: Does not prove every user path.

mechanisms.title: Atomic maintenance cutover for an installed checkout
mechanisms.problem: Maintaining an installed tool by editing the live checkout risks a partially applied, unrecoverable state.
triggers: maintenance is performed on an installed checkout
the launcher points at a mutable branch
obligations: Derive the target from the installed launcher/process environment.
Treat the launched checkout as immutable except for its existing merge lock.
Use one UTC timestamp identity for clone, prepare/staging branches, refs and launcher backup; collisions fail rather than suffix.
Validate in an independent clone, then perform exactly one atomic launcher move.
Pre-cutover failure leaves state unchanged; post-cutover failure restores and verifies the backup; retain rollback artifacts until restart and explicit approval.
steps: Resolve target and create the timestamped clone/branches.
Prepare and validate in a separate clone.
Atomically move the launcher.
Verify the new branch after restart; keep backups until approved cleanup.
Publish upstream separately.

enforcement.trust: Timestamp identity and clone validation are mechanical; restart/approval is human.
enforcement.failure: Any pre-cutover failure aborts without mutation; post-cutover failure restores the backup.
enforcement.exceptions: A concurrent maintenance lock blocks; never force a second cutover.

mechanisms.applicability: Tools installed from a checkout and maintained in place.

migration.strategy: Build the clone/validate/atomic-move sequence before using it on a live install.
migration.implementation: Use a launcher symlink or equivalent single switch and keep a verified backup.
migration.requiredSupport: VCS, launcher indirection, and restart capability.

positive: A validated staging branch is activated with one move and verified after restart.
rejection: A timestamp collision or failed validation aborts without changing the launcher.
recovery: Restore the launcher backup and verify the old branch.

limitations: Not truly atomic on all filesystems.
Single-operator assumption; concurrent edits are out of scope.

mechanisms.title: Calibrated translation as a versioned executable pipeline
mechanisms.problem: Translation quality degrades when prompts are edited ad hoc and outputs are not validated.
obligations: Treat the prompt as an executable asset with its own verifier and request/response snapshot.
Inject only languages and terminology; reject malformed placeholders.
Keep the filename outside the prompt and supply reviewed whole-document pairs.
Declare instruction priority (meaning/structure > terminology > gold-pair voice > general guidance) and require an explicit review pass.
Parse strictly on order, cardinality and envelope; escape reserved delimiters losslessly.
steps: Render the prompt with validated variables.
Translate and return the three-section response.
Parse and validate structure; review terminology and preservation.
Record the snapshot and run prompt tests on changes.

enforcement.trust: Structural validation only; semantic quality needs review.
enforcement.failure: Malformed placeholder or response shape fails before writing.
enforcement.exceptions: Calibration revisions may change examples but must preserve the executable protocol.

mechanisms.applicability: LLM-based translation of structured documentation.

migration.strategy: Freeze protocol and snapshot before tuning wording; version the prompt.
migration.implementation: Separate renderer, prompt asset and parser.

positive: A valid response parses and preserves terminology/structure.
rejection: Malformed placeholders or wrong section count fail.
recovery: Re-render and retry; never write partial output.

mechanisms.title: Briefed minimal translation updates
mechanisms.problem: Re-translating whole documents to update a small region causes preservation collapse and terminology drift.
triggers: a paired document changes on one side
obligations: Brief the translator with the complete working set and deterministically widen context (unit -> section -> document) when needed.
Refuse rather than guess when context is insufficient.
Apply mechanical code-fence-only edits directly and validate against the gate signature.
Scope gate arguments to changed files; keep corpus-wide sweeps in doc-sync/CI.
Make bare `--write` refuse so bulk re-recording is visible; pin exact bytes under content-addressed refs.
steps: Detect changed source regions and assemble the briefing.
Translate only the briefed units or apply fence-only edits.
Validate structure and pairing signature.
Record only changed pairs; run scoped gates.

enforcement.trust: Blind-judged replay evidence supports the update mode; recorded bytes are authoritative for pairing.
enforcement.failure: Insufficient briefing refuses; stale signature blocks.
enforcement.exceptions: A full retranslation may be justified by a document-wide change.

mechanisms.applicability: Maintained bilingual documentation pairs.

migration.strategy: Adopt briefing before allowing partial updates; measure preservation with controls.
migration.implementation: Generate a deterministic briefing and validate against existing pairing records.

positive: A small region update preserves untouched translations.
rejection: A retranslation that drifts unrelated sections is rejected.
recovery: Rebrief with wider context or revert to the recorded pair.

mechanisms.title: User-visible GUI change evidence
mechanisms.problem: PRs claiming user-visible changes ship without reproducible visual proof.
triggers: a PR changes product-user-visible GUI behavior
obligations: Attach a demonstration GIF with real provenance stated beside the embed (real branch tree, real key, real model rounds).
Use a fixture only when the user explicitly requested it.
Publish media to an append-only orphan assets branch, one per PR series, never rewrite/delete.
Use a shallow scratch clone, fixed commit message and raw embed URL; never commit media to the PR branch.
Keep recording side-effect-free; attach only when the task includes it.
steps: Record the real flow from the branch tree.
Publish to the assets branch via a scratch clone.
Embed with `?raw=true` and state provenance.
Review the visual against the changed behavior.

enforcement.trust: Provenance is declared; reviewers must inspect the embed and description.
enforcement.failure: Missing or mislabeled evidence blocks acceptance.
enforcement.exceptions: Non-visual changes; fixture demos on explicit request.

mechanisms.applicability: UI products with reviewable visual behavior.

migration.strategy: Create the assets branch and embed convention before requiring evidence.
migration.implementation: Automate upload/validation; require the link in the PR.
migration.requiredSupport: A media branch and review policy.

positive: A real-flow GIF is attached and matches the change.
rejection: A stale or mislabeled GIF is rejected.
recovery: Re-record from the current branch and replace the embed.

limitations: GIFs do not prove untested paths.

mechanisms.title: Merge-forward checkpoints instead of abandoned merges
mechanisms.problem: When a base branch advances mid-merge, abandoning or rewriting the current merge loses validated work.
triggers: the base advances during the merge
obligations: Finish, validate and commit the current merge; push only if authorized.
Merge the newer base in a separate commit; never abandon or rewrite the checkpoint.
Use a lease-protected rebase only where that alternative is explicitly chosen.
Rerun the relevant checks because the combined tree changed.
steps: Complete the in-progress merge and verify it.
Commit and push the checkpoint.
Merge the updated base as its own commit.
Resolve conflicts and rerun checks.

enforcement.trust: History must remain auditable; reviewers check no force-push rewrote a checkpoint.
enforcement.failure: An abandoned merge or silent rewrite is rejected.
enforcement.exceptions: A deliberate rebase path must be lease-protected and documented.

mechanisms.applicability: Long-lived PRs with merge-forward policy.

migration.strategy: Adopt checkpoint commits and rerun policy before enabling merge queues.
migration.implementation: Document the sequence in the contributor guide.

positive: Two checkpoints remain in history and checks rerun after the second.
rejection: A lost or rewritten checkpoint is rejected.
recovery: Restore from the remote and redo the base merge.

mechanisms.title: Dependency updates with a release-age quarantine
mechanisms.problem: Automated dependency updates can adopt compromised or freshly broken releases.
obligations: Apply a uniform minimum release age (e.g., 30 days) to registry/Actions version updates.
Keep security updates immediate; do not weaken the policy because transitives are fresh.
Exclude vendored sources from version scans; route vendored changes through the manifest sync.
Use labels, normal PR checks and maintainer review; no auto-merge.
Pin the package manager and update one lockfile for the workspace.
steps: Configure grouping/cooldown and labels.
Let the bot open PRs; run full checks.
For a blocked fresh transitive, wait or narrow scope rather than lowering the age.
Merge only after review.

enforcement.trust: The bot is not trusted to merge; release age is a policy control, not proof of safety.
enforcement.failure: Too-fresh release blocked by the age check; failing checks block merge.
enforcement.exceptions: Security advisories bypass the cooldown; vendored packages use the sync procedure.

mechanisms.applicability: Projects using automated dependency updates.

migration.strategy: Enable cooldown and review before auto-merge (which stays off).
migration.implementation: Group workspace updates through one lockfile; pin tooling.

positive: An update older than the cooldown merges after checks.
rejection: A fresh transitive is blocked until the window passes.
recovery: Wait, narrow the update, or take a reviewed exception.

limitations: Release age is not a security guarantee.

mechanisms.title: Generated regions inside owned pages with pairing protection
mechanisms.problem: Generated catalogs drift from prose or overwrite human-owned content; bilingual pairs diverge.
triggers: a generated reference is embedded in docs
obligations: Inject generated content only between explicit BEGIN/END markers in owned pages.
Fail loud in both directions on partition mapping errors (unmapped item, mapped-but-gone).
Keep an independent AST backstop with named, non-stale exemptions; everything rendered must be visible to the scan.
Require byte-identical regions across the pair.
Auto-record pairing only when the write is region-confined; never auto-record prose drift or new pairs.
steps: Render the region from the generator.
Replace only the marked block.
Check both-direction mapping and AST backstop.
Compare region bytes across languages; record only if region-confined.

enforcement.trust: Regions are generator-owned; prose remains human-owned and is never inferred.
enforcement.failure: Unmapped item, stale exemption, or divergent region fails.
enforcement.exceptions: Named exemptions for items the AST cannot see, with staleness detection.

mechanisms.applicability: Docs with generated inventories and translation pairs.

migration.strategy: Define markers and region ownership, migrate flat catalogs, then enable pairing checks.
migration.implementation: Generator writes marked blocks; sidecar records hashes.

positive: Regenerating both languages yields identical regions and the pair records.
rejection: A prose edit or one-sided region change fails auto-record.
recovery: Re-run the generator; resolve prose manually and re-record.

limitations: Marker discipline can be bypassed by hand edits.

mechanisms.title: Coverage instrumentation split without dropping tests
mechanisms.problem: Heavy suites pay instrumentation cost twice while thresholds only need one measured lane.
triggers: the same tests run in multiple gates
obligations: Split one lane into instrumented (owns all thresholds) and uninstrumented (still executes tests).
Inject the environment through the gate, not globally, so local runs are unchanged.
Keep membership and filter/exclude pairing in one roster module.
Require measured files to be covered elsewhere or threshold-excluded; fail loudly on a wrong roster.
steps: Identify tests whose files are measured elsewhere.
Move them to the uninstrumented lane while keeping execution.
Validate membership and threshold pairing.
Measure before/after and keep the threshold lane authoritative.

enforcement.trust: Per-file thresholds make misclassification fail, but only for measured files.
enforcement.failure: Uncovered measured file or mismatched roster fails.
enforcement.exceptions: Explicit threshold exclusions must be reviewed.

mechanisms.applicability: Large test suites with coverage thresholds.

migration.strategy: Measure the tax first, then split execution from instrumentation.
migration.implementation: Create two configs sharing the roster.

positive: All tests still run; thresholds pass from the instrumented lane.
rejection: A roster omission leaves a measured file uncovered and fails.
recovery: Fix membership or move the file back.

limitations: Env injection can diverge from local behavior.

mechanisms.title: Forward-only issue status projection
mechanisms.problem: PR/review events reopen or regress issue statuses and create inconsistent lifecycle state.
triggers: PR or review events update linked issues
statuses have a fixed lifecycle order
obligations: Project phase only forward along a fixed order.
Update only same-repo issues that resolve the PR; never add issues without status.
Never set terminal statuses backward; keep lifecycle projection independent from PR metadata policy.
Accept that late-created issues wait for a later event or manual update.
steps: Map the event to a target phase.
Compare with current phase; apply only if forward.
Run as a separate required check from metadata policy.
Use a focused transition-policy test.

enforcement.trust: One-way by design; no scheduled reconciler.
enforcement.failure: Invalid transition is ignored; the policy test catches regressions.
enforcement.exceptions: Manual update may advance a missed issue; automation never moves backward.

mechanisms.applicability: Issue/PR lifecycle automation with ordered phases.

migration.strategy: Define the order and terminal states, then enable the projection.
migration.implementation: Pure decision function + workflow event hook.

positive: A forward event advances status once.
rejection: A backward event leaves status unchanged.
recovery: Manually advance and let the next event continue.

mechanisms.title: Actionable gate diagnostics for coverage failures
mechanisms.problem: Coverage summaries hide which files/lines are uncovered, forcing manual archaeology.
obligations: Emit one clickable `path:line:col` record per uncovered statement/branch/function in deterministic order, above the threshold summary.
Emit zero output when green.
Wire one reporter for CI, local and focused runs.
Use 1-based columns; degrade gracefully for Infinity spans and implicit branches.
Do not cap the listing when the gate requires zero gaps.
steps: Run coverage with the shared reporter.
Read the actionable records; fix or exclude with justification.
Rerun; confirm clean output when green.

enforcement.trust: Istanbul's data is authoritative; the reporter only formats.
enforcement.failure: Nonzero exit above the summary and uncovered locations.
enforcement.exceptions: A justified CJS exception may load the reporter via require outside the ESM pipeline.

mechanisms.applicability: Projects with per-file coverage gates.

migration.strategy: Replace the summary-only reporter and verify with a planted failure.
migration.implementation: Use the coverage provider's location data; keep deterministic sorting.
migration.requiredSupport: Coverage tool and CI annotation support.

positive: A green run prints nothing; a red run prints clickable locations.
rejection: A failure without locations is rejected as incomplete diagnostics.
recovery: Fix the listed location and rerun.

limitations: Reporter cannot fix ambiguous source maps.

mechanisms.title: Build, pack and exercise release artifacts before publishing
mechanisms.problem: Publishing directly from a build can ship untested, wrong-architecture or uninstallable artifacts.
obligations: Build platform binaries on matching native runners, transfer and assemble the family.
Verify the assembled family, pack immutable tarballs, install and exercise those tarballs before protected publish.
Order platform tarballs before the entry and namespace release tags.
Run an external plain-Node rehearsal proving executable, byte identity and ELF architecture.
Use a bootstrap token only until trusted publishing is available.
steps: Build each platform on its native runner.
Assemble and verify the package family.
Pack and install the tarballs in a clean consumer; exercise the entry.
Only then allow the protected publish workflow.

enforcement.trust: The packed artifact is tested, not the workspace; publication credentials are protected.
enforcement.failure: Missing platform, wrong architecture, failed install/exercise blocks publish.
enforcement.exceptions: Prerelease tags/dry runs may skip publication but still pack and install.

mechanisms.applicability: Native or multi-platform package families.

migration.strategy: Separate build/pack/verify from publish and gate publish on the probe.
migration.implementation: Use native runners and a throwaway consumer.

positive: Packed tarball installs and the entry runs in a clean consumer.
rejection: Wrong architecture or failed install blocks publication.
recovery: Rebuild the missing platform and repack; do not publish partial sets.

limitations: Probe exercises only the entry, not every behavior.

mechanisms.title: Custom merge driver for translation pairing sidecars
mechanisms.problem: Standard text merge accepts one-sided edits or writes unverified pairing metadata.
triggers: a bilingual pairing sidecar is merged
the merge driver runtime is missing
obligations: Install and probe the driver runtime; if missing, let Git text-merge but return a conflict.
Require both owners' three-way merges to be clean and verify switchers/structural signature.
Record merged blobs only when both sides and structure agree; never record one-sided edits.
Fail unresolved for malformed, missing, other-strategy or conflicted cases.
Provide a post-merge resolver that proves the sidecar untouched and worktree bytes equal an independent merge.
steps: Configure the driver for the sidecar path.
On merge, run both owners' merges and validate signatures.
Write blobs only when safe; otherwise leave conflict markers and exit nonzero.
Run the resolver after a clean merge to verify and batch records.

enforcement.trust: The driver is trusted only after runtime probing; it refuses rather than guesses.
enforcement.failure: Conflict/unresolved exit blocks merge.
enforcement.exceptions: Text merge output may remain for humans, but metadata is never accepted unverified.

mechanisms.applicability: Repositories using hash-paired bilingual artifacts.

migration.strategy: Probe runtime before publishing the integration; keep text merge as fallback.
migration.implementation: Register the driver and a verification resolver.

positive: Both-clean merges record the correct paired blobs.
rejection: A one-sided edit or missing runtime yields a conflict, not metadata.
recovery: Resolve manually, rerun the resolver.

limitations: Driver correctness depends on structural signature.

mechanisms.title: Single terminology authority for bilingual docs
mechanisms.problem: Multiple renderings of one contract concept teach inconsistent terminology.
triggers: a paired document uses a domain term
obligations: Keep one binding rendering per concept in a terminology source.
Migrate all active pairs and re-record sidecars; keep archived notes frozen.
Make calibration assets/prompt prose follow the table so they cannot teach a superseded rendering.
Do not rename identifiers, paths, API names or machine-readable values during prose maintenance.
Add a global row only for a real contract term; disambiguate overlapping conventional terms locally.
steps: Look up the term in the table.
Apply the binding rendering in active pairs.
Update calibration/prompt assets.
Run pairing/doc gates and re-record changed pairs.

enforcement.trust: The table is authoritative for prose; identifiers are excluded.
enforcement.failure: Inconsistent pairing or terminology in active docs fails review/gate.
enforcement.exceptions: Archived/frozen docs keep historical rendering; conventional overlaps get no global row.

mechanisms.applicability: Bilingual technical documentation with shared concepts.

migration.strategy: Build the table before bulk translation; migrate active pairs and freeze history.
migration.implementation: Link the table from the translator brief.

positive: A new translation uses the binding rendering and records.
rejection: A superseded rendering in an active pair is flagged.
recovery: Fix prose (not identifiers) and re-record.

limitations: Archived term drift remains by design.

mechanisms.title: Durable citations to committed artifacts
mechanisms.problem: Prose cites session ordinals or uncommitted observations that readers cannot resolve.
obligations: Cite only committed, in-repo-resolvable artifacts (note path/name, doc page path, issue number).
Replace session ordinals with the decision name or delete them and restate facts standalone.
Pin regressions as present-tense counterfactuals; implemented notes state shipped reality.
Exempt fixtures/snapshots/archived notes, but ban indexical stamps everywhere.
Use lexical probes calibrated with positive and near-miss controls.
steps: Resolve every citation to a committed path or stable ID.
Rewrite indexical references into timeless facts.
Run the lexical probe; inspect near misses.
Trace owner-first edits into generated consumers.

enforcement.trust: Probes catch patterns, not semantic invalidity.
enforcement.failure: An unresolvable citation is a review finding.
enforcement.exceptions: Historical/archived notes may contain old paths if marked as historical.
enforcement.knownGap: No gate currently bans new session ordinals automatically.

mechanisms.applicability: Decision records and docs citing sessions or transient evidence.

migration.strategy: Adopt the citation vocabulary, then migrate notes and add probes.
migration.implementation: Use path/ID citations; restate facts instead of pointing to a session.

positive: Every citation resolves in the committed tree.
rejection: A new session ordinal or dead path is flagged.
recovery: Replace with a stable citation or restate the fact.

limitations: No full semantic validation of cited claims.

mechanisms.title: Markdown fragment and rendered-anchor integrity
mechanisms.problem: Headings change, so links with fragments silently point nowhere; source slugs also differ from published slugs.
triggers: docs are rendered to a site
obligations: Validate fragments including same-file links against rendered heading slugs or explicit `<a id>` anchors.
Register anchors only from real HTML flow; code/comments register nothing.
Handle slug rules (inline markup, underscores, occupied-set suffixes, exact case).
Run a post-build verifier over every emitted HTML page; fail on missing page/id, ambiguous routes or malformed hrefs.
Keep source validation independent of the published verifier.
steps: Extract links and anchors from source Markdown.
Validate against source slugs; cache lazily for archived/vendor targets.
Add explicit aliases where renderers disagree.
Build the site and re-validate emitted HTML.

enforcement.trust: Renderer behavior is authoritative for output; source validation remains a separate check.
enforcement.failure: Missing target/anchor fails.
enforcement.exceptions: External, non-Markdown and root-absolute targets are out of scope; explicit aliases cover renderer differences.

mechanisms.applicability: Documentation sites and Markdown link corpora.

migration.strategy: Add source validation, fix existing links, then add the post-build verifier.
migration.implementation: Use the renderer's slugger or explicit aliases; validate emitted HTML.

positive: Valid fragment and explicit alias resolve in source and output.
rejection: A broken same-file fragment fails.
recovery: Fix the heading/link or add an alias.

limitations: Slug algorithms can change with the renderer.

mechanisms.title: Normalize publication identity away from upstream names
mechanisms.problem: Publishing under upstream npm names squats another project's identity and breaks notices/attribution.
obligations: Bulk-rescope into the owning org with a delimited complete-token rule.
Enumerate invisible sites explicitly (property access, name-as-data constants, docs prose) and freeze historical/vendor prose.
Assert the publication set at pack time.
Keep upstream names in third-party notices; exclude removed names from release-age checks.
Provide an idempotent mapping script with `--check`, run in hygiene; replay the script on rebase.
steps: Define the exact old/new token mapping.
Run the mapping script; inspect non-code sites.
Run `--check` for zero residue and every exact edit.
Assert the packed publication set and notices.

enforcement.implementation: mapping script + pack assertion + hygiene check
enforcement.trust: Script covers declared sites; manual review needed for prose/constants.
enforcement.failure: Residual old name or missing edit fails.
enforcement.exceptions: Historical/archived prose keeps the old name intentionally.

mechanisms.applicability: Forked/vendored packages published under a new scope.

migration.strategy: Enumerate all name sites before the bulk edit; make the script reversible and idempotent.
migration.implementation: Token-boundary replacement plus explicit site list.

positive: All active manifests and code use the new scope; notices keep upstream.
rejection: A leftover old scope or missed exact edit fails `--check`.
recovery: Rerun the mapping script and review the residue report.

limitations: Name-as-data sites are enumerated, not discovered.
Prose may intentionally retain old names.

mechanisms.title: Access as a per-release-sequence manifest property
mechanisms.problem: One npm scope contains packages with different intended visibility, and `--access` flags override manifests.
triggers: multiple release sequences share a scope
a new package joins a sequence
obligations: Declare access per sequence in manifests; enforce it with workspace constraints so new members cannot drift.
Never pass `--access` on any publish path.
Use `workspace:^` for compatible ranges and exact `workspace:*` where a binary must match the entry.
State the irreversibility of making a package public.
steps: Set `publishConfig.access` in each sequence's manifests.
Run the workspace constraint gate.
Pack/publish without `--access`.
Verify visibility after publication if applicable.

enforcement.trust: Manifest is authoritative; registry visibility is external.
enforcement.failure: A new member with wrong access or a `--access` flag fails.
enforcement.exceptions: A deliberate visibility change requires a sequence-level decision.

mechanisms.applicability: Monorepos publishing multiple scopes/sequences.

migration.strategy: Assign access per sequence, add the constraint gate, remove flags.
migration.implementation: Manifest field plus workspace checker.

positive: Each member packs with its sequence's access.
rejection: A `--access` invocation or drifted member fails.
recovery: Fix the manifest/flag and repack.

mechanisms.title: Prefix-scoped credentials for asset publication
mechanisms.problem: A generic upload credential can overwrite unrelated objects.
triggers: binary/media assets are published to external storage
obligations: Accept only an allowlisted set of filenames and verify file type.
Write to a fixed prefix with explicit content type and caching; check the response.
Scope credentials to that prefix; keep the assets repo as rollback source.
Reject a generic uploader even if convenient.
steps: Validate names/types locally.
Upload to the fixed prefix.
Verify the response and public URL.
Rollback by restoring from the assets repo.

enforcement.trust: Credential scope is the real boundary; script validation prevents mistakes.
enforcement.failure: Name/type outside the allowlist aborts.
enforcement.exceptions: Adding an asset requires updating the allowlist and prefix policy.

mechanisms.applicability: Publishing assets to CDN/object storage.

migration.strategy: Create a dedicated bucket/prefix and token, then migrate assets.
migration.implementation: Allowlist + type check + fixed headers.

positive: An allowlisted PNG uploads and resolves.
rejection: A non-allowlisted name fails before upload.
recovery: Restore the prior object from the assets repo.

limitations: Cannot prevent a compromised token within its prefix.

mechanisms.title: In-job test partitioning with merged thresholds
mechanisms.problem: One oversized test process wastes wall time; naive sharding duplicates or drops tests and thresholds.
obligations: Partition inside one job/workspace with fixed counts; no elapsed-time auto-tuning.
Build inventory from the test lister, narrowed and with exemptions removed.
Assign by persisted durations with LPT min-heap, heaviest first.
Run one worker per partition with a temp config; reject empty partitions.
Children suppress thresholds and write one blob; the coordinator validates the exact blob set, then one merged run owns thresholds.
steps: List tests and load duration history.
Partition deterministically.
Run children, capture blobs and bounded tails.
Validate blobs and run the merged coverage/threshold pass.
Fail on spawn/signal/missing/extra/merge errors.

enforcement.trust: Inventory comes from the runner; duration history is advisory.
enforcement.failure: Missing/extra blob, failed test or threshold failure fails the gate.
enforcement.exceptions: A failed test still reports via reportOnFailure.

mechanisms.applicability: Large Vitest/Jest-style suites with coverage merging.

migration.strategy: Fix partition counts first, then add history-based assignment.
migration.implementation: Generate per-partition configs; merge coverage centrally.

positive: Every test runs exactly once across partitions and merged thresholds pass.
rejection: Empty partition or missing blob fails.
recovery: Rebuild inventory/history and rerun the coordinator.

mechanisms.title: Release-tag-gated publication of public docs
mechanisms.problem: Documentation deploys from arbitrary branches expose unreleased content and bypass version checks.
obligations: Deploy only via `workflow_dispatch` from a release tag; never from PR/master checks.
Before building, run the same version gate the package release uses (refs/tags, family prefix, version present in tree) with full-history checkout.
Add an environment tag policy plus required reviewers as a second independent layer.
Keep public source links on master because the public mirror advances only at releases.
Keep production docs build covered by PR/master CI.
steps: Dispatch from the release tag.
Run the release:verify gate.
Build docs and deploy through the protected environment.
Verify the deployed version/routes.

enforcement.implementation: tag-only workflow + release gate + environment protection
enforcement.trust: Two independent layers; neither alone is sufficient.
enforcement.failure: Wrong ref/tag or absent version fails before build; environment policy blocks unreviewed deploy.
enforcement.exceptions: A hotfix still requires a tag; never deploy from master.

mechanisms.applicability: Public documentation tied to releases.

migration.strategy: Reuse the package release gate in the docs workflow, then restrict triggers.
migration.implementation: Tag filter + verify step + protected environment.

positive: A tagged dispatch passes verification and deploys.
rejection: A branch dispatch or mismatched tag is rejected.
recovery: Create/fix the tag and redeploy; do not bypass the environment.

mechanisms.title: Generated explicit resolution aliases with completeness assertion
mechanisms.problem: Wildcard path aliases resolve slowly and can silently omit packages when the fallback is removed.
obligations: Generate per-package explicit aliases into a marked region; leave hand-written aliases alone.
Emit only directory-name-matching packages; throw on ambiguous claims.
Delete the wildcard fallback and assert every source-bearing package is mapped.
`--check` names gaps and runs in the static gate.
Preserve JSONC comments; ensure the entry guard is not a silent no-op on Windows/spaced paths.
steps: Generate aliases from the package hierarchy into the marker region.
Run the coverage assertion and drift check.
Fix unmapped packages or ambiguity.
Measure boot impact and state unaffected paths.

enforcement.trust: Generated region is authoritative; the assertion catches omissions.
enforcement.failure: Unmapped package, ambiguous claim or drift fails.
enforcement.exceptions: Hand-written aliases outside the marker are preserved.

mechanisms.applicability: TypeScript/node monorepos with path-alias-based resolution.

migration.strategy: Generate alongside the wildcard, assert completeness, then remove the fallback.
migration.implementation: Marker-based text surgery preserving comments.
migration.requiredSupport: Package manifest walker and resolver tests.

positive: Every source package maps to an explicit alias and boot improves.
rejection: A missing mapping or ambiguous package fails `--check`.
recovery: Fix the generator input or add the package; regenerate.

mechanisms.title: Filesystem-conditional dependency installation
mechanisms.problem: One install strategy fails on a filesystem with different link semantics.
triggers: CI/host workspace uses a nonstandard filesystem
dependency installation fails with resolution errors
obligations: Branch the install step on the detected workspace filesystem (e.g., block-clone only on ReFS; default on NTFS).
Document the underlying mechanism and tool provenance (which pnpm build supports the flag).
Verify the actual CLI flag works; `.npmrc`/env vars may be ignored.
Record the infrastructure dependency and the failure mode when the layout changes.
steps: Detect the filesystem/link behavior.
Select the install flags accordingly.
Run an install smoke that exercises resolution.
Record the runner-image assumption.

enforcement.trust: Detection is environmental; a rebuilt runner can invalidate the assumption.
enforcement.failure: Wrong branch yields TS resolution errors or failed install.
enforcement.exceptions: Only the detected environment gets the special path.

mechanisms.applicability: Cross-platform repositories with filesystem-specific package-manager behavior.

migration.strategy: Add detection and keep the default path for normal filesystems.
migration.implementation: Document flags and tool provenance.

positive: The ReFS runner installs with the block-clone flag; NTFS uses default.
rejection: Forcing one strategy on the other filesystem fails.
recovery: Restore the detected branch or rebuild the runner layout.

mechanisms.title: Fix timeout root causes and align lane budgets
mechanisms.problem: A recurring timeout is masked by raising the budget instead of removing the cost.
triggers: a test lane times out repeatedly
the same suite has a different budget elsewhere
obligations: Trace the root cause and remove the algorithmic cost first.
Prefer explicit threading of loaded data over a hidden second cache.
Align the lane budget with comparable lanes only after the fix.
Pin the environment value in the workflow spec with a negative control.
steps: Profile the failing gate.
Remove repeated work (e.g., O(names x manifests) reload) and verify byte-identical output.
Set the shared timeout budget consistently.
Add a spec assertion and a negative control.

enforcement.trust: Budget parity is configuration; only the root-cause fix changes cost.
enforcement.failure: Spec drift or timeout fails.
enforcement.exceptions: A genuinely heavier lane may need its own documented budget.

mechanisms.applicability: CI lanes with recurring timeouts.

migration.strategy: Fix cost, then align budget, and pin both.
migration.implementation: Thread shared state; set env per gate.

positive: The suite completes within the shared budget after the fix.
rejection: Budget-only change without cost reduction is rejected.
recovery: Revert the budget or fix the remaining hot path.

mechanisms.title: Single owner for project planning metadata
mechanisms.problem: Planning fields stored in two systems create conflicting permissions and stale reads.
obligations: Store planning metadata in one Project field system.
Reject issue-backed fields or wrong types; use Project APIs.
Split credentials by operation: repository token for REST reads, read-only App token for Project queries, write App token only for mutations.
Initialize fields only on the defining event and only when empty; fail closed on field rename/type change.
Document last-write-wins because no compare-and-set exists.
steps: Validate the field schema before writes.
Read with the read-only token.
Mutate with the write token only for lifecycle events.
Test that read paths hold read-only permission.

enforcement.trust: Permission split limits blast radius; no atomic CAS.
enforcement.failure: Wrong field type/name fails closed; insufficient token fails.
enforcement.exceptions: Legacy org fields are prefixed and unread, not migrated.

mechanisms.applicability: GitHub Projects-based planning automation.

migration.strategy: Pick one field system, validate schema, then split tokens.
migration.implementation: Project GraphQL/REST calls with scoped tokens.

positive: Read-only token reads; write token updates only on lifecycle events.
rejection: An issue-backed field or wrong type is rejected.
recovery: Restore the field schema and rerun with correct token.

mechanisms.title: Workspace-wide version coherence gate
mechanisms.problem: A release bump leaves some packages on stale versions, and release-lane checks alone miss drift.
obligations: State the version invariant once by a name predicate matching the bump writer's scope.
Run the check in always-on static lanes, not only the release lane.
Accept prerelease segments when the release writer does.
Treat the gate as necessary but not sufficient: branch protection must require an up-to-date base/merge queue.
steps: Define the predicate and expected version source.
Run the gate on every change.
Fix drifting manifests in the bump change.
Keep branch protection separate.

enforcement.trust: The predicate is authoritative only for named packages; it cannot fix stale bases.
enforcement.failure: Any named package with a different version fails.
enforcement.exceptions: Non-dsh/renamed packages are outside the predicate.

mechanisms.applicability: Monorepos with one shared release version.

migration.strategy: Derive the predicate from the bump writer, then move the check into static CI.
migration.implementation: Read all manifests and compare to the root version.

positive: All named packages equal the root version.
rejection: A stale package version fails even outside the release lane.
recovery: Run the bump writer and commit all manifests.

limitations: Predicate and writer can drift if edited separately.
