mechanisms.title: Evidence-driven performance work
mechanisms.problem: Performance changes ship from intuition, noisy measurements or claims that do not match behavior.
triggers: a performance optimization or budget change is proposed
obligations: Measure before optimizing and attribute with focused profiling plus independently timed endpoints.
Use comparable cold/warm and retained-memory conditions, synthetic workloads and negative controls for tightened budgets.
Keep behavior evidence independent of timing (logs, ordering, cancellation, disposal).
Classify historical claims (merged/superseded/author-reported/estimate) and prefer final diffs/source.
Ship tighter budgets with the optimization; keep the baseline layer independently mergeable.
steps: Capture a baseline with methodology.
Profile and optimize one cause at a time.
Re-measure with controls and state variance.
Verify behavior separately; commit the budget with the fix.

enforcement.implementation: The performance Skill supplies bounded candidate selection and measurement/evidence cards; it adds no benchmark implementation, runtime behavior or CI policy. Each optimization must supply executable measurements and functional evidence at its actual owner.
enforcement.trust: Timing is evidence, not a correctness gate; private data only for inspiration.
enforcement.failure: An optimization without baseline/controls or with behavior change is rejected.
enforcement.exceptions: The source grants no emergency measure-after bypass; current baseline, comparable controls and behavior evidence remain required.

mechanisms.applicability: Any performance-sensitive change.

migration.strategy: Adopt the evidence template and keep budgets separate from correctness.
migration.implementation: Synthetic, committed inputs; document conditions.
migration.requiredSupport: Owner-provided profiling, independently timed relevant endpoints and a stable measurement harness; executable support is not supplied by this Note.

positive: The guidance itself passes document/link consistency and Skill metadata validation; it does not introduce a benchmark or CI gate.
For a real optimization, its owner supplies executable interleaved baseline/controls and independent functional evidence before claiming improvement.
rejection: Single-sample/no-control claims are rejected.
recovery: Revert or remeasure with a proper baseline.

mechanisms.title: Trust predicates and isolation for self-hosted runners
mechanisms.problem: Routing PR jobs to self-hosted infrastructure can expose credentials or execute untrusted code.
triggers: a job is routed to self-hosted/third-party runners
obligations: Require explicit trust predicates: non-Dependabot author, non-fork head repo matching the current repo.
Keep predicates even if repository settings change; ephemeral runners may deliberately drop persistent-VM rules.
Isolate toolcache/install paths inside runner temp and reject installs outside it.
Avoid global links; clean per-job temp state.
Execute routing expressions in a spec with a negative control.
steps: Define trust conditions for the pool.
Add toolcache isolation and a path check.
Test the real expressions, including an untrusted negative case.
Document which jobs are excluded from failover.

enforcement.trust: Repository settings are not trusted to stay safe; predicates are the gate.
enforcement.failure: Untrusted context or path escape fails the job.
enforcement.exceptions: Ephemeral provider runners may skip persistent-VM-specific exclusions.

mechanisms.applicability: Self-hosted CI runners processing PRs.

migration.strategy: Start with no credentials and a read-only job, add predicates, then isolation.
migration.implementation: Use `runner.environment`/actor/head-repo conditions and a temp path assertion.

positive: A trusted same-repo PR runs with isolated toolcache.
rejection: A fork/Dependabot PR or install outside runner temp is rejected.
recovery: Fall back to hosted runners and fix predicates.

limitations: Predicates cannot detect all compromised accounts.

mechanisms.title: Evaluate eligibility before expensive policy work
mechanisms.problem: Every event creates tokens and reads references even when policy cannot apply.
obligations: Evaluate enforcement eligibility before reads or token creation.
Informational references need REST only for policy validation; resolving references must name an actual Issue; PR numbers cannot satisfy or trigger Project validation queries.

Do not extend that read exemption to lifecycle mutation: project-local planning still initializes empty Start Date on opened events for every referenced actual Issue, including informational references.
Use a capability marker in the trusted default-branch checkout to select preflight vs full validation.
Never choose fallback from execution errors.
Prune irrelevant subscriptions and reject no-op reviews before runner allocation while keeping the required check authoritative.
steps: Parse the event and decide eligibility.
Use the cheapest API for informational reads.
Create Project validation tokens only when eligible resolving-Issue checks require them; separately retain opened-only, empty-only planning-field mutations.
Keep the required job/check unchanged.

enforcement.trust: Errors fail closed; they do not silently downgrade.
enforcement.failure: An exempt validation event performs no policy reference/Project validation work; the separate lifecycle planner still owns its authorized mutations. Missing capability preserves the full legacy human path and Bot/App exemption; execution errors never select fallback.
enforcement.exceptions: REST-only informational validation is not an exemption from opened-only, empty-only Start Date initialization.

mechanisms.applicability: Event-driven repository automation with scoped tokens.

migration.strategy: Add a preflight job before token creation, then prune subscriptions.
migration.implementation: Parse payloads and check reference types first.

positive: Informational policy validation uses REST without Project validation credentials, while an opened event still initializes an empty planning Start Date for the same actual Issue through the separate lifecycle owner.
rejection: A PR number cannot trigger a Project query; an execution error does not trigger fallback.
recovery: Fix the event/reference and rerun; keep the required check.

mechanisms.title: Classify dependency sections by distributed content
mechanisms.problem: Manifest sections are chosen by bundling or habit, leaking browser-only packages into installs.
obligations: Classify by distributed content and runtime ownership: browser-only implementations/static inputs/shared React and type-only imports belong in devDependencies; a third-party Host runtime value dependency takes precedence as dependencies. Type-only imports do not create Host runtime dependencies.
Keep Host libraries for dual-face packages.
Disclose licenses for distributed content even when the section is devDependency; resolve through real build configs.
Reject React install leaks in publication checks; keep classification source-based and idempotent.
Make no standalone browser-library support promise.
steps: Trace the browser and Host entries from real build configs.
Assign the minimal correct section.
Run the dependency verifier and publication checks.
Update tests if a classification changes.

enforcement.trust: Build configs are authoritative; bundled content still needs licenses.
enforcement.failure: Misclassified runtime import or leaked peer fails.
enforcement.exceptions: A reviewed export-level classification can permit dependencies.

mechanisms.applicability: Packages shipping browser and Node surfaces from one manifest.

migration.strategy: Derive the roster from build entries, then enforce sections.
migration.implementation: Read manifests and build configs; classify imports.

positive: A browser-only input lands in devDependencies and notice.
rejection: A required Host runtime value import misclassified as development-only fails; a type-only import is kept in devDependencies and is not omitted from both sections.
recovery: Move the section and rerun the verifier.

mechanisms.title: Distinguish pending merge conditions from publisher failure
mechanisms.problem: A commit status conflates an unmet-but-reversible condition with infrastructure malfunction.
obligations: Publish `pending` for draft, insufficient points, or an effective CHANGES_REQUESTED from a write-capable reviewer.
Let a blocking review dominate point totals.
Publish success only when ready, threshold met and no blocker.
Keep publisher operational health in a separate job.
Consumers must inspect description/reviews to distinguish blocker from other pending conditions; the required status still blocks.
steps: Compute points and blockers.
Choose pending/success/error per the matrix.
Write description listing the specific condition.
Keep a separate health signal for publisher errors.

enforcement.trust: Status semantics are a contract; consumers may need details.
enforcement.failure: Unmet condition = pending (not success); bot failure = error.
enforcement.exceptions: A dismissed review or delegation recomputes the result.

mechanisms.applicability: Custom approval/points merge gates.

migration.strategy: Define the status matrix and a separate health check before enforcing.
migration.implementation: Compute blockers independently from points.

positive: Draft/insufficient/blocked publishes pending; ready+threshold+no blocker publishes success.
rejection: A blocking review with enough points still blocks.
recovery: Resolve the condition and rerun the publisher.

limitations: Review state can change during publish.

mechanisms.title: Identify trusted workflows by path, not display name
mechanisms.problem: A publisher trusts a workflow by a mutable display name or incomplete event metadata.
triggers: a workflow_run event triggers a privileged publisher
obligations: Match the exact `workflow_run.path`, not the display name.
Require the `pull_request_review` trigger and a successful run.
Parse the PR number from `display_title` and validate the supplied association.
Reject a stale reviewed head by comparing the current head.
Cover negative cases: numbered names, invalid paths/events, unsuccessful runs, invalid titles, superseded heads.
steps: Validate run path/event/conclusion.
Extract and validate PR identity.
Compare reviewed head to current head.
Publish or fail closed.

enforcement.trust: Path is repository-controlled; display names are not.
enforcement.failure: Any mismatch rejects.
enforcement.exceptions: Moving the workflow requires updating the expected path in the same change.

mechanisms.applicability: Privileged workflows triggered by other workflows.

migration.strategy: Replace name matching with path checks, then add negative tests.
migration.implementation: Validate event payload fields before token use.

positive: Exact path/event/success/current head publishes.
rejection: Renamed workflow, wrong event or stale head is rejected.
recovery: Update the expected path or re-review the current head.

limitations: Path can be reused by a renamed file.

mechanisms.title: Historical precompiled-asset release requirements with external kit ownership
mechanisms.problem: Heavy engines must not compile during ordinary consumer installs/builds. The historical in-tree LibreOffice release design is not a current executable path at the fixed commit; the later independent-kit decision owns actual engine publication.
triggers: a package ships a heavy precompiled engine
obligations: Compile only in an explicit-dispatch release workflow with matching version tag and protected environment.
Give the package its own version and asset-only export; keep source outside the workspace.
No install lifecycle; packaging verifies an existing build rather than compiling.
Tarball carries manifest/assets, source pins, patches, full diff, licenses and notices.
Reject mismatched receipts, modified assets, unlisted files, missing notices or bundled fonts; failure never auto-compiles.
steps: Build the engine once on the target platform.
Record receipts/hashes and licenses.
Assemble and verify the tarball.
Publish via protected dispatch only.

enforcement.implementation: Historical required design: asset workflow plus packaging verifier. Its linked native/libreoffice-wasm package, release workflow and packaging-test files are absent at the fixed commit; the current independent LibreOffice kit owns API/engine qualification and release externally. No portable replacement or target activation is claimed here.
enforcement.trust: Build receipts, source materials and a protected release decision are requirements when this mechanism is activated, not proof that the historical in-tree path exists.
enforcement.failure: Any provenance mismatch must abort without compiling as fallback; missing real qualification/release machinery is a blocker, not a successful or optional first publication.
enforcement.exceptions: The earlier Note's incomplete first publication is a historical limitation, never permission to consume an unqualified artifact. Current Harness does not build/publish kit packages.

mechanisms.applicability: Heavy binary dependencies shipped as packages.

migration.strategy: Preserve release-only compilation and provenance/qualification requirements, while assigning reusable engine builds and releases to the independent owning project rather than resurrecting removed in-tree product machinery.
migration.implementation: For an activated target, require a real independently qualified release, exact dependency version/lock resolution and retained source/license materials. The Skill preserves this migration contract but does not ship the external native engine build/publisher; that implementation remains blocked until supplied and exercised.
migration.requiredSupport: The actual independent engine owner/release artifacts, native qualification, protected publication and verified installed/offline consumer behavior.

positive: Tarball installs without compilation and matches receipts.
rejection: Modified asset/unlisted file aborts.
recovery: Rebuild/repack from the recorded source.

limitations: Asset provenance depends on real build receipts; the source does not establish signed receipts.

The historical native/libreoffice-wasm package, release workflow and package test no longer exist at the fixed commit. The successor kit repository owns engine qualification/releases; first publication and installed/offline qualification are not optional.
This is preserved historical governance plus an explicit migration implementation gap, not implemented automatic support in the Skill.

mechanisms.title: Discoverable-public experimental publication with a private denylist
mechanisms.problem: A private-by-default policy hides experimental packages; a public-by-default policy can accidentally publish private prototypes.
obligations: Default experimental packages to discoverable public publication.
Keep one explicit private denylist with a named owner.
Require both a denylist entry and a private manifest for a private prototype.
Workspace constraints require public manifests to omit `private` and set access public; reject disagreement.
State that publication grants neither stability nor support.
steps: Decide public/private per experimental package.
Set manifest fields accordingly; add denylist entry if private.
Run workspace constraints.
Publish through the normal sequence.

enforcement.trust: Two fields must agree; publication does not imply support.
enforcement.failure: Conflicting manifest/denylist state fails.
enforcement.exceptions: A private prototype requires both changes; no implicit private default.

mechanisms.applicability: Experimental package families with public releases.

migration.strategy: Start from the current publication reality, add the denylist and constraint.
migration.implementation: Manifest checks plus an explicit list.

positive: A public experimental package omits private and sets access public.
rejection: A denylisted package with a public manifest fails.
recovery: Fix both manifest and denylist.

limitations: Public visibility is hard to undo.

mechanisms.title: Durable repository reference forms
mechanisms.problem: Commit hashes and absolute links break across rewrites/mirrors; current files need relative links.
triggers: prose cites a release, PR, run or file
files move or history is rewritten
obligations: History prose cites release tags and PR/run/job IDs; current files use relative links.
Scan tracked plus nonignored new files for hex candidates.
Resolve candidates against the local Git object database and reject only unambiguous commits.
Preserve blob hashes, schema digests and branch-name hex; do not fetch the network.
Do not claim remote tag immutability.

Keep native source manifests pointed at the public source home; during workflow packing project the workflow repository identity into disposable inputs, preserve source manifests, and publish the resulting verified tarballs unchanged. Local packing without workflow context keeps the public metadata.
steps: Classify the reference as historical or current.
Use the allowed form.
Run the reference gate; inspect ambiguous hex matches.
Keep vendor/frozen-note exclusions explicit.
For native packages, prepare disposable workflow packing inputs with the workflow repository identity while leaving tracked source manifests unchanged; verify and publish that exact artifact.

enforcement.trust: Local object DB only; missing objects cannot match.
enforcement.failure: A bare commit hash in maintained prose fails.
enforcement.exceptions: Blob/schema hashes and branch names are preserved by classification.

mechanisms.applicability: Repositories with long-lived docs and rewritten history.

migration.strategy: Define allowed forms, scan with an explicit hex taxonomy, then fix violations.
migration.implementation: Use tracked/nonignored files plus local Git object classification for references; preserve the separate native-packer identity projection in disposable workflow inputs and verify source immutability/tarball identity at the target owner.

positive: A tag/PR reference passes and a relative current link resolves.
Workflow-native packing records the actual workflow repository in the tarball while source manifests keep the public source home; local packing without workflow context keeps public metadata.
rejection: A bare unambiguous commit hash in maintained prose fails.
Workflow packing that rewrites tracked source manifests or changes the artifact after identity verification fails.
recovery: Replace with the allowed form.

mechanisms.title: PR-scoped approval delegation with one-hop scoring
mechanisms.problem: Delegating review authority can be chained, double-counted or leave stale review state.
triggers: a write-capable non-author comments a delegation command
obligations: Allow delegation only between write-capable non-author accounts, scoped to the PR.
Count transferred points once at the sender's weight; never chain.
Dismiss the sender's prior approvals/change requests so native review state matches.
Let the latest surviving eligible command win; require the author's immutable account id for edits; self-delegation or a submitted review restores own decision.
Equal timestamps favor review; later dismissal cannot revive; recompute on edits/deletions.
Filter comments, resolve the live open head, skip closed/merged, fail on missing history; per-PR concurrency.
steps: Parse the command and validate eligibility.
Dismiss sender's prior review state.
Record one-hop delegation at sender weight.
Recompute status on head/review changes.

enforcement.trust: Immutable account IDs and live head resolve identity; policy tests cover the matrix.
enforcement.failure: Invalid/chained/self delegation or stale head is rejected.
enforcement.exceptions: Author edit or a new submitted review overrides prior delegation.

mechanisms.applicability: Custom approval systems allowing reviewer delegation.

migration.strategy: Implement with a pure policy module and exhaustive workflow tests before enabling.
migration.implementation: Persist command decisions, recompute from surviving history.

positive: A valid delegation transfers points once and updates status.
rejection: Chained/self delegation or stale reviewed head is rejected.
recovery: Delete/reedit the command and recompute.

mechanisms.title: Capped author credit in approval scoring
mechanisms.problem: PR author contribution history should combine with an ordinary review without becoming self-approval; it is not reviewer experience credit.
triggers: a PR author has merged contributions in the same repository
author credit approaches its cap or the ordinary-review admission boundary
obligations: Credit the PR author, not the reviewer: min(100, merged PR count in this repository) × 11 / 1000, capped at 1.1.
Stop lookup at 100 matching merged PRs; match the immutable author account and exclude the current PR.
Author credit alone must not satisfy the default two-point threshold; the author's own review remains excluded.
Keep ordinary reviewer points and production-ownership weighting separate from author contribution history.
Blocking reviews still block regardless of score.
Test the exact threshold boundary (e.g., 90 vs 91 merged PRs) and sub-threshold display rounding.
steps: Resolve current eligible reviews, blockers and draft state before lazy author-history lookup.
Count the same author's merged PRs in this repository up to100 and add the capped author credit to reviewer points.
Compare unrounded points with the source tolerance; display rounding must not grant admission.
Publish score/description and keep blockers independent.
Adjust weights only with boundary tests.

enforcement.implementation: The optional tools/github-approval runtime retains source author-weight.mjs and the trusted weighted-approval publisher; activation and app-bound branch protection are still required.
enforcement.trust: Contribution history is not review quality; GitHub account identity and current reviewer permissions are authoritative, and blockers dominate.
enforcement.failure: Incomplete author history, a stalled cursor or invalid API data fails evaluation instead of granting partial credit.
enforcement.exceptions: Drafts, blockers or sufficient reviewer points skip unnecessary history lookup; policy changes require boundary verification.

mechanisms.applicability: Weighted approval systems; weights are project-specific.

migration.strategy: Preserve the author-only formula, same-repository immutable-account lookup and lazy evaluation; keep reviewer weighting separate.
migration.implementation: Use the optional tools/github-approval installer and references/github-approval.md; preserve the source scorer and independently configure trusted publication and native branch rules.
migration.requiredSupport: Complete same-repository merged-PR history, current review/permission APIs, trusted default-branch publication and app-bound required status.

positive: With one ordinary one-point approval and no ownership boost, an author with90 merged PRs remains pending at1.99, while91 reaches2.001 and may pass only without a blocker.
rejection: An author at or above100 merged PRs has at most1.1 points and cannot approve alone, including by submitting their own review.
A write-capable CHANGES_REQUESTED decision remains blocking regardless of author credit.
Incomplete merged-history responses or a stalled cursor must fail closed rather than grant a partial score.
recovery: Restore complete authorized history and add a qualifying independent approval; rerun current-head evaluation without manually inventing credit.

limitations: Merged PR count measures author contribution history, not reviewer quality.
History and platform permission failures remain blockers; local arithmetic tests do not prove live approval or native branch protection.

mechanisms.title: Build provenance carried as one explicit input
mechanisms.problem: Embedding a build version by rewriting tracked manifests dirties the tree and desynchronizes the built artifact from its commit.
triggers: a packaged artifact needs a version
release upload must validate the artifact
obligations: Pass the version as an explicit argument (or a deterministic auto-next index) through packaging, update feed and upload validation.
Never rewrite tracked manifests to stamp a build.
When auto-numbering, query the real feed and discard partial listings so an existing installer is not overwritten.
Record commit and dirty state in every artifact; tag production only after upload and never fail a completed upload.
Read the upload version from the packaging completion record, not a variable.
steps: Resolve the version once from argument/auto index.
Pass it to all packaging outputs.
Write commit/dirty metadata.
Upload; tag only successful clean production builds.

enforcement.trust: The explicit input is authoritative; dirty state is disclosed, not hidden.
enforcement.failure: Missing/ambiguous version blocks; partial feed listing is discarded.
enforcement.exceptions: Test/local builds deliberately untagged.

mechanisms.applicability: Packaged desktop/CLI releases with update feeds.

migration.strategy: Remove manifest rewriting, add an explicit version input and provenance metadata.
migration.implementation: Thread one resolved version; record completion.

positive: A clean-tree build produces an artifact stamped with version+commit and no repo diff.
rejection: An auto index colliding with an existing installer is rejected.
recovery: Rerun with an explicit free version; never overwrite.

limitations: Dirty builds remain possible but untagged.

mechanisms.title: Clean-checkout build reproducibility and packaged-import invariant
mechanisms.problem: A build passes only because stale outputs exist; a clean worktree produces a broken or differently sized artifact.
triggers: a build depends on other workspace outputs
obligations: Make concurrent builds respect prerequisites; run dependent bundles after required outputs exist.
Record standalone versus former workspace byte identity as explicit reproduction/comparison evidence; do not claim an ongoing automatic byte-comparison gate unless one is separately implemented.
Fail on any bare specifier the packaged app cannot resolve across static/dynamic import/require, per target allowlist.
Read module import records, not chunk metadata; state the requirement, not the symptom.
Write no output on rejection.
steps: Reproduce on a clean checkout with clean:false disabled/controlled.
Order the dependent build after prerequisites.
Run the packaged-import invariant with per-target allowlists.
Capture the build-path byte comparison as verification evidence separately from the executable packaged-import guard.

enforcement.trust: Clean-checkout reproduction is the evidence; stale artifacts are not.
enforcement.failure: An unresolvable bare specifier fails the moduleParsed import guard before output/signing; byte differences belong to the explicit comparison investigation, not a source-implemented packaging gate.
enforcement.exceptions: Allowed specifiers are explicit per target (main/preload).

mechanisms.applicability: Bundled applications consuming workspace packages.

migration.strategy: Remove the package from unordered concurrent builds; add the import check.
migration.implementation: Serialize the dependent step and scan module import records.
migration.requiredSupport: Bundler plugin API and clean CI.

positive: Clean and prebuilt checkouts emit identical bundles; imports resolve.
rejection: A devDependency left external fails with the specifier named.
recovery: Add the dependency or fix exports; rebuild.

limitations: Check covers imports, not runtime behavior.

mechanisms.title: Range policy by release family
mechanisms.problem: One dependency range policy cannot serve packages with different release cadences.
triggers: a package joins a release family
obligations: Use exact workspace references for same-release DSH packages and patch-only ranges for independently released vendor/native packages.
Apply by dependency target, never by consumer directory; include root tooling/apps/peers/dev and optional platform deps.
Reject wrong range forms in the workspace gate.
Check emitted versions in packed manifests.
steps: Classify the target's release family.
Declare the matching workspace range.
Run the workspace constraint gate.
Verify packed manifests after changes.

enforcement.trust: Target classification is policy; the gate enforces the declared form.
enforcement.failure: Wrong range form fails.
enforcement.exceptions: A new family needs a policy update, not a directory exemption.

mechanisms.applicability: Workspaces with independently released package families.

migration.strategy: Classify targets, rewrite ranges, then enable the gate.
migration.implementation: Target-based check rather than path-based.

positive: Each target uses its family's range after packing.
rejection: A tilde DSH or caret vendor range fails.
recovery: Correct the declaration and rerun.

mechanisms.title: Advertised runtime range as an installed-workspace contract
mechanisms.problem: The engine range describes source features but undercuts installed dependencies or advertises unsupported dead lines.
triggers: a dependency raises its engine floor
obligations: Derive the floor from both source feature cut-ins and the highest installed dependency engine floor.
Exclude EOL/unsupported release lines instead of advertising them.
Pin CI to the exact floor, not a floating major.
Pin type definitions to the floor line so newer-only APIs fail compilation everywhere.
Move engine range, compatibility matrix and documentation in the same change.
steps: Check dependency engine declarations and source feature support.
Choose a disjoint supported range.
Pin the floor in CI and types.
Update docs in the same change.

enforcement.trust: `engine-strict` installers enforce the advertised floor; non-strict installs do not.
enforcement.failure: CI floor leg fails or types compile but runtime breaks.
enforcement.exceptions: A dependency may be downgraded only with a recorded decision.

mechanisms.applicability: Libraries/apps publishing an engines range.

migration.strategy: Compute the floor from evidence, pin it, then publish.
migration.implementation: CI matrix entry at the exact version; types at the same major.

positive: Floor-version CI and install pass; documented range matches.
rejection: A dependency engine floor above the advertised range fails install/CI.
recovery: Raise the floor and matrix/docs together.

mechanisms.title: Independent serial CI completeness reference
mechanisms.problem: The optimized required aggregate can omit work while still green.
triggers: a gate inventory or dependency graph changes
obligations: Run a serial, no-shard, concurrency-1 reference per host on master pushes.
Keep diagnostic real-kernel matrices outside branch protection.
Measure latency from job timestamps; do not encode targets as `timeout-minutes`.
State platform ownership explicitly and keep external runtime aborts behind a process boundary rather than deleting tests.

Disclose actual capacity: active serial Linux/Windows references use the in-house vm-backup/dsh-win-ci standby pools; hosted macOS is disabled and standard-hosted serial Linux is absent. The desired independence from organization-owned pools remains an unmet portability requirement, not a current property.
steps: Define the complete aggregate without selectors.
Run it serially per host after merge.
Compare with the required PR path; treat differences as evidence.
Accept a documented post-merge detection window.

enforcement.trust: It is an independent oracle, not a merge gate; failures inform rather than block the PR.
enforcement.failure: Reference failure is investigated; it never silently weakens the aggregate.
enforcement.exceptions: Real-kernel/sandbox legs may be master-only.

mechanisms.applicability: High-optimization CI with a single required aggregate.

migration.strategy: Add a duplicated slow path before optimizing the required path.
migration.implementation: Run the complete owner aggregate without selectors at concurrency1 in explicit OS jobs; record active standby-pool dependencies and separately implement/exercise a portable capacity path before claiming portability.
migration.requiredSupport: Master-push CI capacity; the fixed-source active references require in-house vm-backup/dsh-win-ci pools, and a target claiming portable references must provide an actually runnable alternative.

positive: A provisioned serial reference executes the complete aggregate without selectors and reports the actual OS/pool; disabled macOS and absent hosted Linux are not counted as successful executions.
rejection: A gate only in the optimized path is exposed by the reference.
recovery: Add the missing gate to the complete inventory and rerun.

limitations: Source prose retains a portable-capacity objective, but active reference jobs depend on organization-owned standby pools; that source gap is retained, not certified away.

mechanisms.title: Independent release families with registry-driven publication
mechanisms.problem: One pipeline for packages with different cadences republishes unrelated artifacts and cannot retry safely.
triggers: a workspace contains packages with different release rhythms
a release is published or re-run
obligations: Give each family one version baseline, tag prefix, bump sequence and workflow; share no waiting.
Write versions locally and commit them; CI checks and uploads without repository write permission; humans create tags.
Decide each tarball against registry state: absent -> publish; same version + identical integrity -> skip; same version + different integrity -> fail.
Retry with spacing/backoff and re-read the registry after a reported failure.
Preflight dist-tag overrides across every member and reject the whole attempt if any binding is wrong.
Keep pack credential-free on every pull request and master push; publish only via manual dispatch behind human approval and a global concurrency group.
steps: Bump and commit manifests with the lockfile.
Human tags after merge.
Pack the whole family as one credential-free artifact on every PR and master push.
Dispatch publish; repack, verify, and publish each entry in order.
Verify completion in the registry.

enforcement.trust: The registry is authoritative for publication; tags reserve versions but do not prove success.
enforcement.failure: Integrity mismatch, tag binding conflict or missing member blocks the attempt.
enforcement.exceptions: A skipped version is never retagged; a family with no changes may still advance if bytes could differ.

mechanisms.applicability: Multi-family package publication.

migration.strategy: Split families by trigger/version model, then split pack from publish.
migration.implementation: One workflow file per family and a registry-state publisher.

positive: Re-running publish over one artifact skips all packages; a new version publishes once.
rejection: Changed bytes with the same version fail instead of overwriting.
recovery: Bump the version and republish; never force the registry.

limitations: Tags can drift from registry state.
Byte reproducibility is assumed for skip-on-integrity.
Re-running an older set can move `latest` backward.

mechanisms.title: Optional dependencies are never loaded at module scope
mechanisms.problem: A static import of an optional dependency turns an absent capability into a load failure for every importer, and workspace tests never exercise the absent case.
triggers: a manifest declares optionalDependencies or optional peers
a package ships source to consumers
obligations: Never statically import a package the manifest allows to be absent.
Allow type-only/value-erased imports; reject bare imports, value bindings and star re-exports.
Do not offer dynamic `import()` as the remedy; it only moves failure to first use.
Use `createLazyRequire` only for a genuinely required CJS-compatible Host dependency whose initialization is unrelated to startup.
Report the package, the declaration that made it optional, and the two valid exits.
steps: Read each package's own manifest for optional declarations.
Scan shipped source with a bound Program to distinguish type-only erasure.
Reject retained imports; propose type import or restructuring.
Recognize lazy-require literals as runtime edges.

enforcement.trust: Binding resolution is authoritative, not import syntax.
enforcement.failure: Any retained module-scope import of an optional package fails.
enforcement.exceptions: Type-only imports and declared lazy requires.

mechanisms.applicability: Published packages with optional peers/dependencies.

migration.strategy: Convert optional imports to type-only or move loading behind an owned operation.
migration.implementation: Run the gate over shipped source; fix reports.

positive: A type-only import of an optional peer passes.
rejection: A static value import fails with the declaration named.
recovery: Restructure or use lazy require; rerun the gate.

limitations: Dynamic imports are not statically prevented in all forms.

mechanisms.title: Verify the installed artifact, not just the workspace
mechanisms.problem: Workspace installs contain every package, so tests can pass while the published tarball is broken.
triggers: an install or range resolution could differ
obligations: Pack the whole family into one directory and record upload order.
Install the tarballs into a throwaway consumer with an owned npm cache and drive the installed entry.
Reject missing required dependencies; allow omitted optional ones unless they name an excluded package.
Read a directory by contents when it holds cross-sequence tarballs.
Capture npm HTTP diagnostics on failure.
steps: Pack all members.
Create a fresh consumer and cache; install from file specifiers.
Run the installed executable/version probe.
Report registry/cache diagnostics on failure.

enforcement.trust: The probe is deliberately narrow: payload completeness and range resolution, not behavior.
enforcement.failure: Install or entry execution failure blocks publication.
enforcement.exceptions: Optional dependencies may be absent; cross-sequence tarballs are read by content.

mechanisms.applicability: Published package families.

migration.strategy: Add a credential-free pack+install probe to PRs before publishing.
migration.implementation: Use `file:` tarballs and a private cache.
migration.requiredSupport: Package manager and a minimal consumer.

positive: Tarballs install and `--version` runs in a clean consumer.
rejection: Missing files or unresolvable internal ranges fail.
recovery: Fix `files`/ranges and repack.

limitations: Does not exercise a real registry.

mechanisms.title: Dependency sections follow published artifact ownership
mechanisms.problem: Source-directory coupling puts browser/type relationships into install-time dependency sections or exempts whole package groups.
triggers: a package imports another workspace package
a package joins or leaves a special group
obligations: Classify by published face: client/type-only/metadata-only -> devDependencies; Host runtime value import -> dependencies only if duplicate-safe or export-classified; shared-identity exports -> peer + dev.
Select packages mechanically (client directory plus an explicit marker) with narrow, reviewed include/exclude/host lists.
Reject unknown, stale, redundant, duplicate, overlapping or ineffective policy entries.
No group-level exemption: experimental packages follow the same rules.
Scan worker/child-process entries declared by build configs, not guessed source patterns.
Run on source manifests without built output; block `--fix` while any export is unclassified.
steps: Read source manifests and declared build entries.
Classify each imported export.
Assign the minimal section and range.
Run the verifier; fix or document policy changes.
Run the deterministic two-release layout check; keep timing benchmarks manual.

enforcement.trust: Source and build config are authoritative; the verifier cannot see banner-injected imports.
enforcement.failure: Unclassified import or misdeclared range fails; no writes while violated.
enforcement.exceptions: Reviewed export/package classifications and explicit config-only dev edges.

mechanisms.applicability: Monorepos publishing packages with multiple build faces.

migration.strategy: Start from build entries and export classification, then enforce sections.
migration.implementation: Policy module with explicit overrides and a fix mode.

positive: A Host runtime import lands in dependencies; a type-only import in devDependencies.
rejection: An unclassified export blocks all fixes; an experimental peer browser import fails.
recovery: Classify the export or change the source relationship, then rerun.

limitations: Host-only package coverage is an explicit roster.
Editing policy changes the installed graph.

mechanisms.title: Explicit, scoped CI runner failover
mechanisms.problem: A failover switch silently changes where correctness lanes run, coupling them to unrelated outages or trust boundaries.
triggers: a third-party runner option is evaluated
obligations: Make failover an explicit writer-managed variable, never the default; re-run affected jobs instead of merging.
Scope each switch to named participating jobs.
Exclude credential-holding, release-shaped, spec-pinned benchmark and host-capability jobs from third-party failover.
Keep correctness lanes off unrelated failover state; a failed experiment returns to hosted runners.
Re-validate throughput and failure reproducibility on the actual pool before routing; record constraints for future attempts.
Pin routing in workflow specs and drill the fallback.
steps: Define the participating roster and exclusions.
Set the variable and re-run affected jobs.
Verify scheduling and isolation behavior on the failover image.
Unset the variable to return to default; record gaps.

enforcement.trust: Variable state is repository-writer controlled; provider independence is not guaranteed by config.
enforcement.failure: Unavailable pool or wrong routing fails the job; no silent fallback is assumed.
enforcement.exceptions: A correctness lane may stay hosted permanently; dormant legs require a drill.

mechanisms.applicability: CI with multiple runner pools/providers.

migration.strategy: Add the variable and roster behind default-off, drill, then document the runbook.
migration.implementation: Per-job runner expressions and specs.

positive: With the variable set, only listed jobs move and pass their isolation checks.
rejection: Credentialed/release jobs stay hosted; a failing pool does not become the default.
recovery: Unset the variable and re-run on hosted capacity.

mechanisms.title: Parallel artifact lanes joined before promotion
mechanisms.problem: Parallel packaging lanes mutate shared inputs or promote partial outputs when one lane fails.
triggers: two artifacts are produced from one build
a tool mutates the artifact during signing/notarization
obligations: Give each lane an independent immutable copy when tooling mutates it.
Write and verify configuration explicitly when a packaging hook is skipped for the chosen target.
Wait for both lanes before error propagation and cleanup.
Promote the artifact set only when both lanes succeeded and feed/config checks passed.
Write the completion record last so existing upload validation rejects incomplete releases.
Use isolated output directories to avoid concurrent metadata writes.
steps: Assemble and sign one source artifact.
Copy for each lane; verify config per copy.
Run lanes concurrently.
Join; verify both results and config.
Promote and write completion last.

enforcement.trust: Each lane's own verification plus the join gate; tests use barriers and negative controls.
enforcement.failure: Any lane error or config mismatch leaves the completion record absent.
enforcement.exceptions: A directory-only build may skip one lane but still notarize its App.

mechanisms.applicability: Multi-artifact release pipelines.

migration.strategy: Isolate copies, add explicit config, then enforce the join and completion record.
migration.implementation: Barrier-based tests and a final promotion step.

positive: Both lanes overlap, produce valid artifacts, and promotion occurs.
rejection: One lane fails -> no promotion and no completion record.
recovery: Rerun the failed lane; stale artifacts are not promoted.

limitations: Single timing sample cannot attribute speedup.

mechanisms.title: Per-root schema change acknowledgement
mechanisms.problem: A digest detects schema changes but not whether they are safe, and a global digest invalidates unrelated reviews.
triggers: a writer version or reader behavior changes
obligations: Normalize the transitive type graph; exclude source locations, aliases, comments and property order from structural identity.
Bind each acknowledgement to the affected root's after schema and chain predecessor -> successor.
Classify conservatively: optional additions/required-to-optional/ordinary event additions are same-version; other changes need an explicit same-version decision or a header bump.
Require reader-behavior evidence for same-version: old readers resume, safely ignore optional features, or refuse required features before execution/mutation/tail repair.
Every structural difference needs an acknowledgement explaining both reader directions and executed checks; generators never invent explanations or test results.
Freeze accepted machine records/checkpoints; archived format references derive from the writer constant.
steps: Generate the normalized before/after inventory.
Classify or record an explicit decision.
Write the acknowledgement with verification evidence.
Run the checker; finalize a checkpoint when accepted.

enforcement.trust: Checks prove current-tree consistency, not that history was never rewritten or that explanations match runtime.
enforcement.failure: Unacknowledged change, stale chain or missing header bump fails.
enforcement.exceptions: Ambiguous alternatives stay additions/removals; opaque/unknown structures remain undetectable.

mechanisms.applicability: Persisted formats with compatibility guarantees.

migration.strategy: Adopt normalized inventories and per-root records before changing the format.
migration.implementation: Codec/reader tests plus recorded after schemas.

positive: An optional addition is auto-classified and acknowledged; current source matches the terminal record.
rejection: A required-field removal without decision/bump fails.
recovery: Add the acknowledgement or bump the header and re-record.

mechanisms.title: Prove optional packages stay outside the default product
mechanisms.problem: Public availability or a release smoke containing every tarball does not show what the default product requires.
obligations: Follow runtime dependencies, optional dependencies and peers from every app/runtime, resolving aliases.
Compose the effective configuration with the production patch engine; check disabled rows and patched include trees too.
Check both bundling-stage input graphs and the final HTML graph.
Verify the installed packed graph from the product entry.
Run runtime startup and client activation smokes with a real experimental negative control.
Only declared optional bundles are exceptions; missing default roots fail.
steps: Run the dependency/source-composition checks.
Run build-input checks for each bundling stage.
Install/pack and traverse the product graph.
Boot real Host/Chromium smokes and inspect registries.
Review declared exceptions.

enforcement.trust: Multiple independent layers; a negative control proves the checks can detect a violation.
enforcement.failure: Any path introducing an optional package into the default entry fails.
enforcement.exceptions: Launcher `OPTIONAL_BUNDLES` and separate previews outside the default graph.

mechanisms.applicability: Products with optional/experimental plugin families.

migration.strategy: Define the default entry and exceptions, then add layers from source to runtime.
migration.implementation: Reuse the production patch/composition engine.

positive: Optional package remains reachable only via explicit opt-in; default product starts without it.
rejection: A negative-control experimental plugin mounted by default fails the smoke.
recovery: Remove the edge or declare an exception explicitly.

limitations: Does not cover every later user-triggered path.
Computed-path patches can escape static discovery.

mechanisms.title: Split artifact emission from complete diagnostic ownership
mechanisms.problem: Every artifact job rebuilding aggregate test/script programs duplicates expensive diagnostics and invites removing them entirely.
triggers: multiple CI jobs need compiled packages
obligations: Keep complete aggregate checks in required normal builds and public build/typecheck.
Let artifact builds compile all project references but omit only each root's extra test/script programs.
Use `--noCheck` emission only where another analyzer owns semantics, and record pending checks so later incremental builds still diagnose.
Prove both paths reject package errors and compare emitted JS/declarations/maps/build-info with fixtures.
Transfer aggregate checks to another blocking owner before deleting a full build.
steps: Measure the duplicated cost.
Introduce the artifact path with the same references and ordering.
Add ownership documentation and fixture checks.
Keep required full builds until a replacement owner exists.

enforcement.trust: Emission equivalence is fixture-backed; full diagnostics remain with the required build.
enforcement.failure: Package error on either path or byte divergence fails.
enforcement.exceptions: Benchmark-only noCheck emission with pending-check bookkeeping.

mechanisms.applicability: CI with repeated compiled-artifact consumers.

migration.strategy: Add the split path without removing diagnostics; prove equivalence, then use it for consumers.
migration.implementation: One serial `tsc -b`, omit only root extras.

positive: Artifact and full builds emit identical package bytes; full build still diagnoses aggregate errors.
rejection: An aggregate-only error is missed by the required path or bytes differ.
recovery: Restore the full check or fix the artifact compile.

limitations: Artifact path intentionally skips aggregate-only diagnostics.

mechanisms.title: Lossless performance optimization with byte and diagnostic parity
mechanisms.problem: Optimizations silently change emitted bytes, diagnostics or behavior while reporting a speedup.
triggers: a tool behavior is changed for speed
obligations: Establish a baseline and use interleaved variants with same-code controls and multiple samples.
Prove output bytes identical (hashes across representative files) and the diagnostic set unchanged.
Declare any intentional behavior/diagnostic-ownership change separately and document the new owner.
Add a guard for each optimization and a negative control that fails when the guard is removed.
State RSS, critical-path and measurement limitations.
steps: Capture baseline with methodology and spread.
Apply one change at a time.
Compare bytes/diagnostics and record costs.
Add/pin guards and negative controls.
Re-measure before claiming the gain.

enforcement.trust: Byte equality is strong evidence; single-host timings are not production proof.
enforcement.failure: Byte/diagnostic difference without a declared behavior change blocks.
enforcement.exceptions: An intentional ownership transfer is allowed when documented and covered.

mechanisms.applicability: Compiler/bundler optimization work.

migration.strategy: Measure, optimize losslessly, guard, then document trade-offs.
migration.implementation: Hash outputs and diff diagnostics; keep controls.

positive: All output hashes match and the gain exceeds control spread.
rejection: A byte/diagnostic change without declaration is rejected.
recovery: Revert the item or document the ownership change and update guards.

limitations: Not all output paths are comparable.

mechanisms.title: No top-level await in importable package source
mechanisms.problem: Top-level await makes module evaluation asynchronous and turns entry failures into module-loading failures.
obligations: Use an explicit `async function main()` for entry initialization.
Define failure behavior: exit code, stderr, readiness signal and cleanup.
Gate module-scope `await`, `for await` and `await using` with an AST rule across all nested top-level constructs.
Exclude only bins, identified from declarations (`#!` or manifest bin target), and pin the exclusion list.
Add corpus guards for empty/missing source sets and register the gate in shared hygiene.
steps: Refactor the entry to main().
Run the AST gate.
Handle startup failure explicitly and test it.
Keep bins documented as exceptions.

enforcement.trust: AST scope analysis is precise for syntax; dynamic patterns may evade.
enforcement.failure: Any module-scope await outside bins fails.
enforcement.exceptions: Executable bins; documented scope exclusions (third-party/apps).

mechanisms.applicability: ESM/CommonJS packages imported by other modules.

migration.strategy: Convert entries first, then enable the gate with bin exclusions.
migration.implementation: AST visitor using nearest function body.

positive: An `await` inside main() passes; module-scope await fails.
rejection: A bin exception is honored; a non-bin entry fails.
recovery: Move async work into main() and rerun.

limitations: Banner-injected or generated code may escape.

mechanisms.title: Supply-chain drift, advisory and license verification (proposed)
mechanisms.problem: Forward vendoring enforcement does not verify that the manifest's claims are true, and npm dependencies lack advisory/update monitoring.
obligations: Reconstruct vendor source from the recorded SHAs plus checked-in per-modification patches and fail on unexplained diff.
Scan advisories on a schedule and on lockfile-touching PRs.
Assert license files and manifest license fields against the inventory.
Propose small dependency-update PRs that ride the full gate suite; exclude vendored packages and use the sync procedure.
Keep acceptance criteria and credential risk explicit.
steps: Convert logged modifications to patch files.
Add the nightly drift job, advisory scan and license check.
Configure update proposals.
Treat a blocked private-mirror job as a local scheduled task.

enforcement.trust: Not implemented; do not claim automatic enforcement.
enforcement.failure: Planned: unexplained diff, advisory, missing license fail.
enforcement.exceptions: Vendored updates excluded from automated dependency PRs.

mechanisms.applicability: Projects vendoring source and publishing dependencies.

migration.strategy: Implement license check first, then drift, then advisories/updates.
migration.implementation: Patch files + scheduled jobs.

positive: Planned: reconstructed vendor tree matches; license inventory passes.
rejection: Planned: unexplained diff or advisory fails.
recovery: Planned: update manifest/patches or dependency.

limitations: Classification choice for advisory scanner deferred.

mechanisms.title: Generate package/gate inventories instead of static lists (proposed)
mechanisms.problem: Static package and gate lists duplicate manifest/layout facts and drift with every new package.
triggers: a package or gate is added
aggregate references or docs repeat inventories
obligations: Use one canonical source (package hierarchy plus manifests) for aggregate references, module graph and full-package lists.
Pair generation with a `--check` staleness gate in hygiene/doc-sync.
Make doc-sync the single command that owns and prints sub-gates; docs link rather than restate.
Keep static lists only where they encode policy.
Keep discovery boring: read manifests, filter explicit fields, print results, fail loud.
steps: Generate references/inventories from the hierarchy.
Commit generated artifacts.
Run `--check` in CI.
Delete hand-maintained duplicates.

enforcement.implementation: generator + --check gate (not yet adopted as described)
enforcement.trust: Proposal; existing module-graph/catalog generators show the pattern but do not prove this inventory is generated.
enforcement.failure: Planned: stale committed copy fails.
enforcement.exceptions: Policy lists remain hand-authored.

mechanisms.applicability: Large monorepos with repeated inventories.

migration.strategy: Start with aggregate references, then unify doc-sync sub-gates.
migration.implementation: Generator + check mode.

positive: Planned: adding a package regenerates all inventories with no manual list edit.
rejection: Planned: stale committed inventory fails `--check`.
recovery: Planned: regenerate and commit.

limitations: A previous wildcard-paths attempt was reverted for runtime cost.

mechanisms.title: Periodic dual-reviewer maintenance from human review feedback (proposed)
mechanisms.problem: One-off audits of review feedback are inconsistent, and merge/thread-resolution or author 'fixed' replies are not proof of adoption.
triggers: a skill/review guidance needs maintenance from review history
obligations: Use an out-of-repo periodic tool against a clean refreshed default branch; scan idempotently with no repository cursor.
Require merge-commit reachability; skip individual bad PRs; fail loud on search caps.
Accept only human-authored feedback with creation/last-edit strictly before merge; never use merge, thread resolution or author replies as adoption.
Build PR-specific before/after snapshots so target-branch-only changes appear in neither.
Require two independently configured reviewers to agree on author and adoption, then on candidate/covered/specific/not-feedback; fail closed on schema/id errors.
Draft from structured agreed guidance, never raw text; keep adapters tool-free/read-only; both reviewers approve the same diff in a bounded loop.
Reject out-of-target/staged edits before and after gates; roll back with best-effort CAS; write only the single target and never auto-merge.

steps: Availability preflight: this package ships the proposed protocol, not the private scanner, reviewer adapters, scheduler or promotion helper. Record missing prerequisites and stop this workflow before acquisition or drafting; do not report an unavailable run as 'no candidate'.
Scan merged PRs in the overlap window.
Collect eligible human feedback and adoption evidence.
Run dual author/adoption review, then dual candidate classification.
Draft, review the same diff, run docs/lint.
Promote via draft PR after operator inspection.

enforcement.implementation: Source-specified private periodic tool and adapters, outside the fixed source checkout; no executable implementation of this proposed workflow is shipped by this package.
enforcement.trust: Fail-closed evidence rules; adapters run with scrubbed env and nonce-tagged untrusted text, but access/tools are contract markers, not a sandbox.
enforcement.failure: Any unresolved/ambiguous item is excluded; no valid batch result exits nonzero instead of 'no candidate'.
enforcement.exceptions: Merge/thread/author replies are context only; singleton candidates allowed.

mechanisms.applicability: Protocol/reference for maintaining review guidance from repository review history; not a currently runnable workflow in this package. The source Note remains proposed despite its source-reported partial observations.

migration.strategy: Retain the complete proposal and its acceptance bar without advertising an executable workflow. Before activation, the target maintainer must supply or implement the private acquisition, evidence, dual-review, candidate and promotion components and verify them against this protocol.
